Title: Provision of Continuous Attitude Surveys to Defence Medical Services
Description:
The Headquarters Surgeon General  is responsible for conducting the Defence Medical Services (DMS) Continuous Attitude Surveys (CAS).  Surveys are conducted for serving military DMS personnel (both regular and reserve) employed within the MOD.  They are used to provide management information to the Defence Medical Services Board and the Personnel Policy Working Group.

As part of various initiatives within the DMS, the key research objective is to identify areas for development that can help inform future HR strategic policy decisions across DMS, including the single Services Medical; Branches.

The Supplier is required to:
1. Produce and deliver, using the most appropriate means, a self-completion questionnaire for on average approximately 10,000 military medical personnel to complete with a method of return to the Contractor within an agreed timeline.  The questionnaire should contain no more than 100 attitudinal questions, 5 non-standard questions, 12 demographic questions and up to four opportunities for open comments.  The sample strategy will be directed by the Designated Officer (DO).

2. Conduct statistical and trend analysis from results over a 3-year period (2016 - 2018).

3.  Provide final reports in hard copy format (2 copies) and soft copy format (1 copy) and data analysis comparator tool in electronic format (licences for 3 people to access the tool) to the DO, 3 weeks prior to the results presentation. 

4. Produce PowerPoint presentations of headline results in a house style agreed between the Contractor and the DO for up to four presentations.  These presentations will then form the verbal feedback from the Contractor to the Authority. 

5. Provide up to 6 days on-site support to the Authority during the survey period to assist with the administration of the survey.

•	Whether UKSA's current threat assumptions are reasonable and properly informed 
•	Whether UKSA's security risk assessment is comprehensive; covering risks to people, assets, information and processes and is up to date.

Title: GB-Bristol: SHIPACQ197 - The Supply of a Representative Model of a QEC Platform
Description:
There is a requirement to provide a representative model of a Queen Elizabeth Class (QEC) Aircraft Carrier platform for use in steady state training at the Royal Navy School of Flight Deck Operations.  This model is needed to help train Aircraft Handlers to plan and conduct aircraft movements within and on QEC platforms in preparation for sorties and recovery operations. These training aids must be fully representative of QEC flight deck, hangar, operating/safety systems and aircraft, that can be utilised visually and physically during Aircraft Handler career training.
      
      The flight deck scale is a priority and shall include correctly painted markings and lights. The model must be 400-500cm in length and have a removable flight deck. The construction material is unspecified, but shall be a material that is hard wearing and can be painted and repaired. Representative aircraft, vehicles and personnel shall also be included.

The locker shall have an Inline Inductor assembly attached to the left of vertical side of completed assembly and will consist of:
      
      Inline Inductor

      Male adapter
      
      Two nozzles and four size 3 hoses are also required.

Title: Tempus Pro Specialist Support - Defence Medical Security Accreditor and Business Analyst
Description:
This is a direct award contract through G-Cloud 10 CCS Framework no RM1557.10.

Summary of Work - Defence Medical Security Accreditor/Capability Developer (SAC)
The SAC shall produce Technical development work to include security and JSP604 accreditation to enable Tempus Pro data transfer over MoD and Civilian bearers, and data connectivity for up to 100 Tempus Pro devices to Force Elements @ Readiness. To provide Technical support for the establishment of Response Centres.
Specific objectives are:
•	Continuation of SAC activity in FY19/20 including SAC support to JSP604 activity.
•	Develop Codes of Connection (CoCo) for connections for TP to military basebands.
•	Develop Target of Accreditation for RLI-based Corsium Suite using MedIS 1U Server.
•	Limited support to capability development events including TSI generation.
Essential Skills and experience:
•	Recent experience providing Security Accreditation Co-ordinator services to a Defence Communications project.
•	Be a ISO 27001 Lead Auditor
•	Be a member of CISSP
•	Experience as a SIRA

Summary of Work - Business Analyst
The medical device is fully accredited for standalone information storage. The Business Analyst will be required to develop this documentation, with the help of the project team, to achieve approval for network connectivity.
Specific objectives are:
•	Undertake JSP604 compliance activity on behalf of Authority, for Amazon Web Services-hosted Corsium.
•	Advise on ISS approvals and scrutiny process, including liaising between multiple ISS project teams.
•	Manage up to 6 capability events.
•	CONUSE, use case and User Requirements Document development, including two hosting solutions.
•	Future Med IS (CORTISONE) coherence activity.
Essential Skills and experience:
•	Recent experience producing a full requirements document set for a UK Defence communications project.
•	Experience of data flow analysis, IER production and architectural mapping to facilitate JSP 604 accreditation.
•	Experience of utilising Agile Business Analysis methodology.
•	Clear understanding of current UK tactical and strategic data basebands/bearers.

Contract Value Breakdown
Security Accreditor: £93,130 ex. VAT (134 days at £695.00 per day)
Business Analyst: £111,200 ex. VAT (160 days at £695.00 per day)

Title: ISS Service Integration Partner (SIP)
Description:
ISS is the organisation within the Ministry of Defence (the "Authority") responsible for delivering the Defence Information Strategy, through the design, development and operation of information and communication technology ("ICT") across the Authority. In line with this strategy, ISS is moving away from current high-value and complex contracts to a more cost-efficient 'Defence as a Platform' ("DaaP") model. 

The DaaP model will enable ISS to move from the current high-value and complex contracts to a more cost-efficient platform model with common architecture across all services, enabling smaller and more agile contracts to be placed. The DaaP contract structure will also involve suppliers of DaaP services working together collaboratively. This requirement will be supported by a binding collaboration agreement which will set out a range of objectives and principles designed to encourage and facilitate collaboration among suppliers. 

The DaaP model also anticipates that ISS will build upon its existing in-house DaaP Services Integration Office ("DSIO"). The DSIO is a core team that manages, tracks and intervenes in ISS projects and programmes for the delivery of, and changes to, specific ICT services ("ISS Projects") in order to ensure overall integration and coherence of ISS ICT services. DSIO also ensures that any incoherencies with delivering end-to-end ISS ICT services are appropriately identified, documented and managed. 

SIP role and responsibilities 

The Authority now wishes to procure an ISS Service Integration Partner (SIP) to support DSIO and bring about the step-change in capability required to deliver the full benefits of the DaaP model, and manage an increasingly complex multi-sourcing service landscape. 

The SIP will augment and support the DSIO to ensure the requisite integration and coherence of the design, development and delivery of all DaaP services, through multiple transition states and ultimately into live service. 

This will include (without limitation) the SIP delivering the following services to ISS and the Authority: 

a) delivering and maintaining a transparent, robust and coherent transition state model to ensure the viable delivery of ISS services; 

b) ensuring all multi-sourced components of the Authority's ICT estate are integrated and remain coherent throughout the complete service development lifecycle, supporting the delivery of end-to-end ISS services that meet the Authority's expectations and designated performance levels for ISS Services; 

c) supporting a 'one team' approach for the delivery of ISS services where all parties collaborate effectively and work towards shared outcomes; and 

d) delivering a comprehensive knowledge transfer, upskilling and training programme to ensure that the DSIO is able to perform such service integration activities in-house in the future.

Title: Provision of Emergency Airfield Cover for Boscombe Down Aerodrome
Description:
Emergency Medical provision required

Within 10 Minutes  of an emergency call the contractor will provide:

Airfield Incident

a.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

Off-Site Incident

b.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

Domestic Incident on Boscombe Down

c.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

The Emergency Medical Airfield cover

This will consist of several elements including:

a.	Provision of Pre-Hospital Emergency Care and Treatment.
b.	Participation in all on and off (as determined by the exercise and training plans in conjunction with DPHC) site exercising and training events as directed by the Fire Master.
c.	Participation in the creation and generation of paramedic and technician response to major incident plans for the Airfield at MOD Boscombe Down as directed by the Fire Master.
d.	Regular review session with the Military Aviation Medical Examiner (MAME) Medical Officer responsible for MOD Boscombe Down based at the Bulford Medical Centre. 
e.	Support to the airfield in the management of aircraft and air personnel first aid kits destruction.

For a full description and how to apply for this opportunity please refer to the attachments to this Notice

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DSTL, Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (DSTL)
Title: SERAPIS Framework
Description:
In order to maximise the impact of Science and Technology (S&T) for the Defence and Security (D&S) of the UK, Dstl's role includes the responsibility for leading the formulation, design and delivery of a coherent and integrated Ministry of Defence (MOD) S&T programme using industrial, academic and government resources. In particular, the Cyber and Information Systems Division stewards both the Cyber and the Command, Control, Communications, Computer, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities (including Space).  The Defence and Security Analysis Division stewards the Synthetic Environment and Simulation capabilities.
      
      The Serapis Framework aims to provide an expedient mechanism for Dstl to access industrial and academic expertise both within the UK and wider, in support of the Divisions' S&T programmes, and potentially wider MOD and Partner Across Government organisations (PAGs). The construct should allow the supply base to be refreshed throughout the contract lifespan, ensuring that Dstl has access to innovative solutions and robust technical support. Such a construct will allow for the rapid response to emerging capability needs, Urgent Operational Requirements / Urgent Capability Requirements (UOR / UCR) and surge requirements emanating from operations.
      
      Based on the structure and contents of the programmes and the aggregation of wider requirements across the portfolios, the Serapis Framework has been categorised into six Lots, details of each Lot is provided in this notice.
      
      The competition is seeking to appoint a Prime Contractor for each Lot to lead, manage and deliver research in to the areas covered by the six Lots.  The appointed Prime Contractors will be responsible for delivering agile, and cutting-edge research, building and maintaining a robust supplier network with an emphasis on scientific excellence, innovation, and collaboration to exploit research, skills and capabilities. 
      
      In addition to Dstl and the Ministry of Defence (MOD), the Serapis Framework will be available to the following Government Departments / Public Authorities (including their agencies and public bodies): the Home Office, the Foreign & Commonwealth Office and the Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy.

Title: GB-Gloucester: MOD Medal Laser Engraving Machines - Purchase Option-No.2
Description:
The MOD Medals Office has a requirement for two compact pulsed fibre laser engraving machines and two PCs with screens, keyboards and appropriate software to operate the machines in accordance with the specification. Please note that the MOD have also placed a Contract Notice advertising this requirement as an option to have two engraving machines provided as a service. The requirement is also for the installation of the equipment, operator training and a preventative maintenance and support package to cover the laser engraving machines, the PC hardware and software and which will include a Customer Helpline with availability from 08.00 to 16.30, Mon to Fri. 
      The laser engraving machines will be required to:
      •   engrave a range of medals and awards made from a variety of metals including but not limited to Sterling Silver, Cupro Nickel and Rhodium plated Cupro Nickel;
      •   engrave centrally around the rim of circular and oval medals with thicknesses that range between 3mm and 6mm; 
      •   engrave both flat and concave surfaces in both straight lines and circles without damaging the surfaces of the medals:
      •   engrave between 25 and 30 circular and oval medals per hour and work for approx. 8 hours per day (upto 6 days a week);
      •   engrave details provided on a USB stick as a delimited text file and or a xml file (.csv would not be acceptable as the "comma" would be included in the engraving details).
      Full details of the requirement can be found in the Statement of Requirement which is contained in the Invitation To Tender (ITT) Document which is available under the supporting documents on Defence Contracts Online (DCO) (see www.contracts.mod.uk) and can be accessed from the Response Manager page using - Access Code 9U46NRU95T.

      Suppliers interested in this requirement should complete Parts 1 and 2 of the on-line Suitability Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) including the Declaration using the DCO and submit it electronically by 11:00 on Thu 30/05/2019. Suppliers should also complete their tender, as detailed in the ITT Document under supporting documents on the DCO and should also submit it (via post or courier) to arrive by 11:00 on Thu 30/05/2019. The SAQ details the grounds for rejecting Requests to Participate and the minimum levels of capacity and capability that are required to perform the contract.

Title: DInfoCom/0069 - Provision of Digital Project Support for Armed Forces Recruiting Programme
Description:
The Armed Forces Recruitment Programme (AFRP) is a Category A, Government Major Projects Portfolio programme, responsible for the delivery of a single, common Tri-Service Recruiting Operating Model (ROM) for the Army, Navy and RAF from March 2022 onwards.  The Programme started life in March 2018 as an Army programme; the Defence Board directed that AFRP become Tri-Service in December 2018.  Whilst this offered the opportunity to achieve value for money through increased buying power and improved efficiency from a common approach, it significantly increased the complexity of the programme and the risk to delivering the Mandate.  As a strategically important programme for Defence and in light of the current recruiting problems faced by all three Services, there is significant political and senior leadership interest in the programme. 

The requirement is for the "Digital Project", which will be responsible for identifying and documenting the data requirements of the new Tri-Service ROM.  This will involve capturing the data, investigating and articulating customer and user needs, translating these needs into requirements to deliver the digital Statement of Requirement which might be delivered through the existing or a new digital solution.  The recruitment system is the core critical business application and the products generated from this package of work will steer the high-level evidence-based decision for the future Armed Forces digital recruitment environment.

The Cyber Risk Management Function (part of the MOD's Cyber Security Operations Capability (CSOC)) requires a set of tools that will allow for automation of the ingestion, storage, analysis and exploitation of Cyber risks, and informing data, to keep pace with the increasing level of cyber risks being discovered. The Cyber Risk tooling capability is required by September 2019 to fall in line with programme expansion and roll out. This Design Phase is to scope what can be delivered by this deadline.

Additional support is required to fulfil the Design Phase of the project, ensuring that an appropriate solution is defined that will offer a stable foundation and scalable configuration for the growing cyber risk management capability, while providing immediate benefit to users. The foundations will allow for the ingest of all cyber risk-related data such as threats, vulnerabilities, cyber events and incidents data. This will also permit rapid broadening of the data import, analytics and data exploitation capabilities, which will allow the MOD to understand its cyber risk exposure and the prioritised risks that need treatment.

Ministry of Defence - primarily the Cyber Risk Management Team in C4ISR & Cyber Joint User and the Defence Assurance and Information Security (DAIS) team, with growth across the MOD in time. 
The user's need includes a design for an automated method of ingesting, storing and analysing of Cyber Risks based on an existing big data platform.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, Land Equipment, Other
Title: Challenger 2 Life Extension Project
Description:
For the avoidance of doubt, this Contract Notice and Dynamic Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (DPQQ) are being released in advance of a formal approval of available funding to initiate a competition. This approach is intended to accelerate the subsequent release of an Invitation to Negotiate (ITN) to the pre-selected field of bidders once approval to proceed to competition has been confirmed. For planning purposes only the Authority is assuming that formal approval will be achieved in late January 2016.
      
      The UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) Armoured Vehicles Programmes (The Authority) has a possible future requirement to deliver a Challenger 2 Life Extension Project (CR2 LEP). The user requires the CR2 Main Battle Tank (MBT) Out of Service Date to be extended from 2025 to 2035, in order to continue to provide precision direct fire manoeuvre capability across a broad spectrum of operations. CR2 LEP seeks to address obsolescence issues to maintain main battle tank capability until 2035. This is a Category A Military Project (up to £700M inclusive of VAT, including initial logistic support).
      
      Subject to internal approvals, the Authority intends to conduct a Competitive Negotiated Competition under the Defence Security and Public Contracts Regulations 2011 with the intention of inviting a minimum of three tenderers. From these tenders the Authority intends to utilise Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) principles to down select to two Prime Contractors, with each being invited to independently undertake a 2 year Assessment Phase (AP) under contracts not to exceed the Authority's total AP budget of £42M inclusive of UK VAT. The ultimate aim of the competition will be to award a Demonstration, Manufacture and In-service Support (DMI) contract to the bidder which at the conclusion of the AP provides the most economically advantageous tender for the DMI contract.   
      
      During the AP the Authority will negotiate with the AP contractors under the Competitive Negotiated Procedure to refine their specific DMI proposals which will be evaluated at the conclusion of the AP. The Authority will then select a winner who, subject to a Main Gate investment decision, will deliver their proposed DMI solution in accordance with the terms included in the ITN and resolved during the AP. The ultimately successful DMI contractor will be required to formally undertake the role of Design Authority (DA) for the whole Platform. The timing for establishing formal DA status would be co-incident with the successful achievement of Critical Design Review during the D&M Phase.  
      
      Industry should note that the Invitation To Negotiate (ITN) will require the AP contractors to consider support options for any new to service items in conjunction with the Authority's primary Support provider (Babcock DSG Ltd), which is the existing provider of support to the Platform (and its common based platform variants) via existing Inventory and Repair Contracts. Title: EA to Conduct Preferred Choice Modelling Analysis for Armed Forces People Programme
Description:
Requirement - The Armed Forces People Programme requires "stated preference" modelling to understand the likely impact on recruiting and retention of Service (military) personnel of a number of options for a new package of financial and non-financial rewards (the "New Offer"), and of new contract terms that will allow Service Personnel to work part-time or to limit their liability to be moved around the country or overseas.
Background - The United Kingdom's 2015 Strategic Defence and Security Review (SDSR) undertook to "enable our Armed Forces to work more flexibly, reflecting the realities of modern life"  and to "develop a new Armed Forces offer for new joiners".  The Armed Forces People Programme's mission is to deliver the commitments made in SDSR. Its vision is to create "a modern and inclusive Armed Forces which attracts, retains and values its people, in order to enhance operational capability, offering choice as to how they live and work, and providing a comprehensive and sustainable reward package that recognises their commitment and service."

Title: Overseas Deployable Food
Description:
The MOD contracted out the requirement for the supply of food in the early 1990's. Since 2006 that requirement has largely been met by the World Wide Food Services Contract. It is now inteneded to split the requirement into four separate contracts covering: the supply of food within the UK; dog food; in-flight catering and the supply of food to overseas locations. The overseas element will be met by this contract, the Overseas Deployable Food Programme (ODFP).] 
      The Overseas Deployable Food Programme  requirement aims to deliver a cost effective, fully optimised, low risk feeding capability to meet the requirements of the British Armed Forces and entitled personnel for all areas within scope, in accordance with the agreed UK, EU and Defence applicable quality and sustainability standards. 
      The term of the contract is 5 years with the possiblity of 2 x 1 year options available at the discretion of the Authority, with an approximate maximum value of £150,000,000 . It is estimated that the cost of food will account for approximately 30% of this, with non-food costs (logistics capabilities to source, store and transport the food) accounting for approximately 70% of the value of the contract . 
      The potential provider shall manage the supply chain to source and deliver fresh, ambient, chilled and frozen food products from core ranges of approximately 1000 lines (which may vary depending on location and scope).  A representative example of the tyrpical types and range of products is as follows:
      Fresh vegetables and salad - cauliflower, cucumber, onions, leeks, fresh herbs, broccoli and potatoes.
      Ambient - canned Ham, tuna chunks in brine, mushy peas, canned red kidney beans, canned fruit cocktail, sultanas, cereals, apple juice tetrapack, biscuits, tea bags
      Chilled - cheese, eggs, margarine, butter, milk, meat products (beef striploin, beef mince, lamb leg, pork leg)
      Frozen -  Pork and beef sausages, cod, fish fingers, ice cream, bacon, ice cream
      
      They will also be required to provide inflight frozen bricks, for a limited range of inflight meals, to locations as directed by the MOD.
      
      There may be a requirement for the potential provider to provide, at six months notice, a catering function in support of enduring stabilisation operations, for example the provision of Chefs and associated supporting staff.
      
      Delivery of food will be to permanent and exercise locations overseas as directed by the MOD (static and greenfield), including: the British Forces South Atlantic Islands, Kenya, and overseas operations that potentially could be in hostile and remote locations. Examples of recent regular Exercise locations have included, but are not limited to: Norway, USA, Spain, Denmark, Germany and Oman.
      
      The potential provider must also be able to provide personnel to manage and operate out of the MOD warehouse situated on the Falkland Islands.

Description: Sports-event organisation services.  The Authority has a requirement for a 1 year contract with option for a further year for the provision of a venue, services and facilities for Telemark Titan ski training and racing competition hosting up to 170 personnel for up to 15 days in January each year.  The contractor will be required to provide a championship venue that is able to conduct Telemark ski racing events, which must be on mainland Europe, and no more than 1200km from Calais, and no further than 2 hours drive from an International airport and have good public transport links.  The Contractor will be required to provide suitable slopes for teaching beginners through to race techniques, prior to the delivery of a race programme that will meet FIS Telemark regulations requiring a jump, a loom (and large banked turn) and a suitable skating area in the finish.  All dedicated race slopes/courses are to meet Federation International Ski (FIS) standards and be homologated for GS.  And race slopes should take a maximum of 20 minutes to get from the finish area back to the start area by the use of lifts; ideally 10 minutes or less.  An area to run a 'mountain race', with ascent and descent (both on and off piste) in controlled conditions is also required.  Suitable medical and mountain rescue support is required to support the training and racing, as are homologated timing systems and appropriate safety provision and netting.  A suitable race office is to be provided with the ability to connect to broadband internet and conduct administration.  A suitable location for 150 personnel to attend a prize giving is also required.  Facilities for racer's personal ski preparation are required.  Accommodation for all personnel will be required in the local vicinity - tenderers will be required to put forward suggested accommodation solutions as part of their tender.  Provisional Championship dates are 2018 - Jan 2018; 2019 - Jan 2019. Description:
The 3SST2015 is a strategically important programme for STFC RAL Space and UK (via UK Space Agency and UK Ministry of Defence) with key milestones which must be met if UK is to achieve its objectives and deliver its commitments in this international programme.

The 3SST2015 is part of the SST-Framework which will continue until 2020 when it will be succeeded by the SST-Programme.  

The UK Government (with the UK Space Agency [UKSA] leading) is coordinating UK's activities to meet the SST Consortium objective.

The aim of this tender is to contribute to the EU SST WPs 4-6 in order to enable STFC ( a sub-contractor to UKSA, the UK Beneficiary to the H2020 grant which makes STFC a Third Party subcontractor in the EU's H2020 framework) to fulfil their commitments to UKSA.

This tender comprises of specific work requirements within the Space Situational Awareness (SSA) area  in order to deliver the deliverables identified within the 3SST2015 project. It concerns the technical Work Packages only - WP5, WP6.  

The work is mostly concerned with the Work Package 5, UKSA is leading Work Package 5 at the EU level while STFC is leading Work Package 6 at the EU level.  STFC is providing support to Work Package 4 UK lead. The delivery of the requirements specified will enable STFC to fulfil its commitments for Work Packages 4, 5 and 6.  The work relating to WP4 is limited to liaising with the WP4 Leader with respect to the interfaces and technical tasks co-ordination between WP4, WP5 and WP6. 

Please refer to the attached documentation for the full specification.

Title: GB-GLASGOW: HOCS3b/00055 - Provision of DDC News Press Management System
Description:
1.	Directorate of Defence Communications (DDC) is  the central communications directorate of the Ministry of Defence which provides policy and guidance on defence-wide media and communications. 
      The DDC News manages all media contact and currently has a requirement for an on-line database to log and manage media enquiries, collate interview requests for ministers and to forecast upcoming issues.
      
      The News Team within DDC operates a 24 hour a day service to domestic and international media 345 days a year. Each and every day the majority of the news team will interact with national, regional and trade journalists and are required to provide a timely and accurate service in order to fulfil the department's strategic communications objectives. 
      As one of the busiest communications teams in Whitehall, DDC News will issue numerous statements, provide guidance on a wide variety of subjects and will process interview bids for Ministers and senior members of the military every day. In order to do this it is imperative that there is a system in place that logs journalist interaction and provides a database for all statements that have been issued. This allows consistency in messaging and allows individual members of the News team who may not specialise in one subject area to access information and respond to enquiries quickly.
      
      The News Team currently uses a single word document to save all media statements and attempts to save core scripts on the shared MOSS site. This comes with limitations as a shared word document does not allow the news team to log individual contacts with journalists and, as lines evolve and change, it often causes confusion when trying to find statements devoid of background and context in a single word file.  
      Using a single word file has led to individual members of the News team trying to find statements that have been issued in previous media coverage rather than through our own systems. This is because the single word file for 2016 consisted of 600 pages making it very difficult for lines to be found. It is currently not uncommon for one member of the News team to have to phone the Communications Officer who dealt with original request for information to get clarity on the latest line to take and to get the background on an incoming media enquiry. This can often happen out of hours and during the night which is clearly not acceptable.
      Given the lack of certainly with previously issued statements, there is concern that an individual communications officer could unknowingly issue an out of date line or provide a journalist with incorrect information due to a lack of a central resource to log and store statements DDC is therefore seeking a new platform in which all media interaction can be logged..

Title: DE-Bielefeld: CB/BFG/0122 - Provision of Services and Facilities for Exercise Telemark Titan Events 2018-2019 *Duplicated*
Description:
The Authority has a requirement for a 1 year contract with option for a further year for the provision of a venue, services and facilities for Telemark Titan ski training and racing competition hosting up to 170 personnel for up to 15 days in January each year.  
      The contractor will be required to provide a championship venue that is able to conduct Telemark ski racing events, which must be on mainland Europe, and no more than 1200km from Calais, and no further than 2 hours drive from an International airport and have good public transport links.    
      The Contractor will be required to provide suitable slopes for teaching beginners through to race techniques, prior to the delivery of a race programme that will meet FIS Telemark regulations requiring a jump, a loom (and large banked turn) and a suitable skating area in the finish.  All dedicated race slopes/courses are to meet Federation International Ski (FIS) standards and be homologated for GS.  And race slope should take a maximum of 20 minutes to get from the finish area back to the start area by the use of lifts; ideally 10 minutes or less.  An area to run a 'mountain race', with ascent and descent (both on and off piste) in controlled conditions is also required.  
      Suitable medical and mountain rescue support is required to support the training and racing, as are homologated timing systems and appropriate safety provision and netting.  A suitable race office is to be provided with the ability to connect to broadband internet and conduct administration.  A suitable location for 150 personnel to attend a prize giving is also required.  Facilities for racer's personal ski preparation are required.   Accommodation for all personnel will be required in the local vicinity - tenderers will be required to put forward suggested accommodation solutions  as part of their tender.
      Provisional Championship dates are
      2018 - Jan 2018
      2019 - Jan 2019
      
      At the tender stage there will be a requirement for the Evaluation Team to visit the site to verify the evidence provided in the Tender responses during the Tender Evaluation period.  The dates for the site visit are currently expected to be between 06-10 February 2017.

Title: Maritime Multi-Link (MML) Phase 2 Training Needs Analysis (TNA) Technical Assistance
Description:
The Maritime Multi-Link (MML) programme aims to replace the existing Beyond Line of Site (BLoS) Link 11 system with Link 22. Link 22 has been developed within NATO since the late 1980s and can be referred to as the NATO Improved Link Eleven (NILE) system. It will interconnect air, surface, sub surface and ground based tactical data systems, so that Units can share their tactical pictures in Near Real Time[1] (NRT) and at distances BLoS. The long-term aim is to achieve a pan-fleet Link 22 capability installed on multiple platforms

The requirement is to conduct targeted elements of Training Needs Analysis (TNA) to support the development of steady state training for The MML operators and maintainers that will allow personnel to Operate, Maintain, Diagnose and Repair (OMDR). It also provides direction on how the TNA should be carried out, and provides details of some of the key issues and considerations that must be made in its conduct. The TNA will inform the transition timescales from interim OEM training to steady state training to be delivered for MML.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, Ships, Maritime Platform Systems (MPS)
Title: Marine Systems Support Partner
Description:
Platform Systems (MPS) team, which is part of the Ships Operating Centre within Defence Equipment & Support organisation, provides global support to Royal Navy and Royal Fleet Auxiliary ships and submarines. 
      In planning for the future, the Ships Operating Centre is driving forward a Common Support Model, transforming support delivered to all complex warships by a converged, high performing, cost effective support model underpinned by a common approach to class, design and equipment management.  The aspiration is to have the Common Support Model in place in time to support the Queen Elizabeth Class Aircraft Carriers and Type 45 Destroyers from the end of November 2016.  
      As part of the Common Support Model, MPS is planning to transform its organisation structure and ways of working from equipment to systems lines, by implementing its new Marine Systems Hub (MSH).  To support its implementation of the MSH, and in view of the timelines to support QEC/T45, MPS is considering contracting for one or more Support Partners, who will be responsible for working alongside the MOD team to provide a range of services covering spares, systems repairs and post design services (including provision of technical SQEP) for maritime platform equipment. The support will primarily cover T45 and QEC but legacy equipment may be incorporated in the future, and as appropriate, future warship and submarine platforms in the Fleet. 
      In view of the diverse nature of the equipment MPS has described this requirement as 4 systems - Power & Propulsion; Environmental, Domestic & Habitability; Platform Systems; Mechanical & Constructive; allowing a maximum of four contracts to be placed. A single contract may be placed if all four systems are awarded to one company as they provided the Most Economically Advantageous Tender for each System.
      The potential contract/s will be placed with Platform Systems Support Partner(s) who will be required to undertake Engineering and Logistics support activities for T45/QEC Systems and Equipment and will discharge these responsibilities as part of the Systems Technical Authority (STA).  The role of the STA is to provide guidance and advice to the MPS Systems Approving Authority (SAA), who has responsibility for ensuring system integrity on behalf of the Platform Safety Duty Holder.  
      
      The STA will provide assurance to the SAA:
      •	that design change has been holistically integrated into the relevant system; 
      •	provide evidence-based assurance to the SAA that the solution meets the Design Intent at the system level; 
      •	Supports Ships OC Duty Holders in diagnosing system failures and providing an emergency response service to the Navy on constraints to be placed on operational activity when using systems outside their design intent; and 
      •	Identifies opportunities for improvement of system design.
      
      In some instances the Authority may consider delegating the equipment approving authority role to the STA.

Title: Technical Support to the UK Link 16 Frequency Clearance Agreement
Description:
This contract Link 16 Frequency Clearance Agreement (FCA) Technical Support is essential to maintain the FCA and includes the requirement to provide technical expertise. 
The Situational Awareness and Command and Control Delivery Team (SACC DT) is responsible for maintenance of the UK Frequency Clearance Agreement (FCA).  This agreement between the UK MOD and the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) defines the acceptable levels of Link 16 transmissions that are permissible in the UK Flight Information Region (FIR).  The agreement exists because Link 16 is an unauthorised user in the 960-1215MHz Frequency Band that is allocated to civilian Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS) equipment, and as such Link 16 is only permitted to operate on a tolerable interference basis.
The FCA forms part of an overall Frequency Clearance Agreement Safety Management System (FCA SMS) that underpins all Link 16 use.  FCA SMS maintenance is fundamental to the continued safe use of Link 16 in the UK FIR and this SOW defines the technical support activities required to maintain and support this.

Title: GB-Glasgow: JFC7A/00027 - HELMINTH / PARASITE TESTING FOR GURKHA RECRUITS.
Description:
JFC7A/00027 - HELMINTH / PARASITE TESTING FOR GURKHA RECRUITS > The Authority has a requirement for a contract to provide Helminth / parasite testing to approximately 270 Ghurkha British Army recruits per annum. The British Army recruits Ghurkha soldiers into the Infantry Training Centre each February, and the well-being and health protection of the Ghurkha forces is critical to the operational output of the Infantry Training Centre.       There is a high prevalence of helminths / parasites, including strongyloide, in the Ghurkha population, with approximately 25% of Ghurkha recruits to the British Army affected.  Traditionally these were treated with a single dose of albendazole, however an MOD research study found that several parasites residing within the gastrointestinal tract were resistant to albendazole therapy, therefore requiring stool and serum analysis to identify specific parasites and allow the provision of targeted, bespoke treatment.        In addition, the presence of helminth infection has been associated with false negative IGRA tests to exclude latent tuberculosis infection. The implications therefore are that a small proportion of those incorrectly diagnosed with helminth infection will go on to develop active TB, therefore adding even greater importance to the testing process.      The Contractor will be required to provide helminth/ parasite testing and results to the Authority within designated timelines.   
      Duration 3 years plus 2 x option years dependent upon future MOD needs & / or Contractor Performance.

Title: GB-High Wycombe: Enabling Contract for the Provision of Link 16 Advance and Network Design Training for UK JDLMO
Description:
1.	The requirement is a Firm Price Enabling Contract for two (2) Years (1 April 2015 – 31 March 2017) with a further two (2) One Year Options (1 April 2017 – 31 March 2018 & 1 April 2018 – 31 March 2019).

2.	The UK Joint Data Link Management Organisation (JDLMO) is the sole UK authority on the planning, design, coordination, management and execution of data links activities in support of National, NATO and Coalition operations within the UK and Out of Area. To deliver these outputs the JDLMO is dependant on extremely specialized and highly qualified staff within the data link domain. To ensure that its personnel have these necessary skill sets the JDLMO provides a variety of training tailored to meet its particular requirements.
The JDLMO mission is achieved through three distinct areas. Firstly, the Network Design Cell (NDC) who are responsible for collating Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) from the Link 16 participants and achieving the complex task of designing a network and allocating timeslots accordingly that meet these IERs. In addition the NDC is also responsible for converting network designs from other design facilities for use by UK platforms. Secondly, the Plans department, made up of long term plans and short term plans are responsible for production of the weekly Op Task Link (OTL) signal, JTIDS Forecast Activity report JFAR and JTIDS Co-ordination Message (JCM) as well applying for Clearance to Operate (CTO) and Clearance to Radiate (CTR) for all UK platforms participating in overseas exercises utilising Link 16. Finally, the Network Management Cell (NMC) who are responsible for the day to day running of the UK Link 16 Networks as well as policing the UK Frequency Clearance Agreement (FCA) on behalf of the CAA. In addition, the NMC provides a deployable capability to be able to dynamically manage Link 16 Networks in a theatre of operations.

3.	The requirement is for an enabling contract to deliver up to 15 days of Defence Systems Approach to Training (DSAT) Compliant TDL training per year which will include;
 
	The first 3 days will comprise Link 16 Advance Training and will accommodate up to 30 students per day.

	This will be followed by 12 days of Network Design, Planning and Management training and will accommodate up to 12 students per day.

	The contractor shall provide the necessary resources including training notes and stationary. The training will be delivered at RAF High Wycombe or another facility deemed appropriate by the JDLMO. 

	In addition extra training amounting to up to an additional 20% on top of the 15 Training days (i.e. 3 days) to allow the delivered training to evolve to meet the JDLMO’s emerging training requirements and on a "continuous improvement" basis iaw DSAT quality system i.e post course evaluation.  

4.	In the event of a high number of Expressions of Interest a possible Pre-Qualification Questionnaire may be used.

Title: GB-Bristol: Ion Chambers
Description:
The Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Delivery Team (DT) has a requirement to procure quantity seven 1000cc spherical ion chambers to support tertiary level calibration of Radiation Detection and Monitoring Equipment (RDME) used within the Ministry of Defence (MoD). The authority currently uses the Unidos electrometer model type 10002, therefore the ion chambers required must be compatible for use with this instrument. 

The chambers must meet the following specifications:

1.	Ion Chamber Type: Guarded (Air Equivalent) Vented.
2.	Connector Type: TNC (Male) 
3.	Volume: 1000cc
4.	Sensitivity: ≥40 µC/Gy
5.	Collection Efficiency: ≥99%
6.	Mounting: Rigid Stem
7.	Measurement Range: ≤0.1mSv/h to ≥0.3Sv/h
8.	Energy Range: 40 keV to 1.3 MeV (≤±4% across the range)
9.	Directional Dependence: ≤+0.5% (for rotation around the chamber axis - ≤±5% (for tilting the axis up to ±45 degrees)
10.	Short Term Stability: Readings taken within 2 hours after warm-up shall be within  ±0.5% of those taken directly after warm-up
11.	Long Term Stability: Readings taken over a prolonged period of operation shall be within ±1% of those taken directly after warm-up
12.	Post Irradiation Leakage: Signal to drop to 1% within 5s after irradiation.
13.	Leakage Current: ≤10fA
14.	Maximum Bias Voltage: 500V (positive / negative potential) Nominal +/-400V
15.	Polarity Effect ≤±1%
16.	Extension Cable: 10m (TNC Female to TNC Male)
17.	Cable Leakage: ≤1pC/(Gy.cm)

Each ion chamber must be accompanied with a check source and fixture to enable a geometrically reproducible location of the source.

The Contractor shall be responsible for:

1.	The manufacturer of seven identical 1000cc ion chambers.
2.	The delivery of the chambers.

Notice Identifier: Transparency Notice of ITN Issue: HQLF4A/005
Title: Transparency Notice of ITN Issue: Provision of Services & Facilities For Exercise Rucksack Events 2016-19
Description:
This notice serves to announce the issue of an Invitation to Negotiate following publication of Voluntary ex ante transparency notice 2015/S 036-061850 dated 17.02.2015. It is not to seek expressions of interest in a new opportunity.

Sports-event organisation services. Recreational, cultural and sporting services. Provision of a venueand facilities for Exercise RUCKSACK, the GBR army and inter-service cross country and biathlon skichampionships for 200 athletes and 40 officials.
The Authority has a requirement for a 1 year contract with options for a further 3 years for the provision of across country and biathlon championship venue with a biathlon stadium and range, which must be on mainlandEurope, no more than 1 200 km from Calais, no further than 2 hours flight time from London and have goodlocal train and bus links to the Stadium.
The biathlon Stadium and Range must be an International Biathlon Union (IBU) ‘A’ licence facility that hostsworld cup and/or world championship biathlon events, on the IBU race calendar. The biathlon stadium and range must have a 30 lane, 50 m, electronic target, biathlon range which is available for training 3 days prior tothe 1st race and for the duration of the championships.
The contractor is to provide full access to the biathlon stadium and range which must have a minimum of a 5 kmloop with floodlights, snow cannon and stockpiles of snow; with the ability to maintain the loop to FIS and IBUracing standards, if snow conditions are poor. On range emergency mountain rescue is to be provided for eachrace.
The Contractor will be required to arrange and manage accommodation for 2 800 bed nights for competitors inlocal self-catering apartments within 5 km of the Race Office and 450 bed nights B&B for Authority Officials inlocal hotels within 800 m of the Race Office.
A Biathlon Race Office (with telephone communications and broadband) is to be provided, central to the Venueand within 800 m of all Hotels used by Championships Officials and Visitors.
The contractor is to produce a compilation of seeded race start lists and deliver a complete results service inaccordance with Army Winter Sports Association (AWSA) Race Rules.
A FIS Technical Delegate, IBU Technical Delegate and Chief of Course for all Cross Country and Biathlon racesare to be provided by the contractor. They must speak fluent English.
One Range Team (x 12 personnel) to manage the electronic targetry is to be provided by the contractor and anIBU Range Referee who must speak fluent English.
A waxing facility, medical facility, commentary room, refreshment and store rooms is to be provided by thecontractor with outdoor (standing) and indoor (seated) prize giving for 250 personnel in a location central to theVenue.
Championship dates are 20.1.-5.2.2016 with Authority Officials arriving 18.1.2016. These dates will vary +/- 5days for future option years if taken up.

Description:
This notice serves to announce Contract Award following the publication of Voluntary Ex Ant Transparency Notice 2015/S 036-061849 dated 17.02.2015. It is not to seek expressions of interest for a new opportunity.
The Authority has a requirement for a 1 year contract with options for a further 3 years for the provision of venue, services and facilities for Alpine and Nordic competitions hosting an estimated 560 competitors (260 Alpine and 300 Nordic) and 40 Authority officials per year.The Contractor will be required to provide a Championship venue in a suitable location that is able to conduct both Alpine and Nordic competitions. If weather conditions such as poor visibility, high winds or lack of snow prevent an event from taking place a reserve location is to be provided by the Contractor in time to deliver the event; which must be within 45 minutes driving time from the primary resort. The Nordic competition must be held on suitable cross country ski courses that meet FIS standards with a dedicated biathlon facility for safety and competition. The biathlon competition must have a 30 lane, 50 m, biathlon range, including penalty loop.Parking, waxing facilities, medical assistance, snow making facilities, timing, toilets, refreshments and emergency medical evacuation must be available. If weather conditions are poor such as lack of snow and poor visibility then Cross Country and Biathlon competitions must have a minimum of a 5 km loop available. Description:

Recreational, cultural and sporting services. The Authority has a requirement for a 1 year contract with options for a further 3 years for the provision of a venue, services and facilities for snowboarding competitions hosting up to an estimated 160 competitors per year.
The contractor will be required to provide a championship venue that is able to conduct Parallel Giant Slalom, Snowboard Cross, and Freestyle events, which must be on mainland Europe and no more than 1200 km from Calais, no further than 2 hours from an international airport and have good local train and bus links. Under the change programme, the DE&S organisation has been established as a Bespoke Central Government Trading Entity within the public sector from 1 April 2014, with new management freedoms and controls that are appropriate to its challenges and the specialist nature of its business.

Requirement

The MSP will be a key provider of the services/requirements driving the Materiel Strategy change programme. Potential MSPs should note that the DE&S is planning to appoint other MSPs for two further Work Packages – Work Package (WP) 1, Project Delivery to transform and improve the operation of its project delivery capability and Work Package (WP) 2, Finance/Management Information/Information Technology (Fin/MI/IT) to transform and improve the operation of its financial and information management capability.
Within the boundaries of the freedoms and controls given to DE&S as a Trading Entity and working with the MSPs of WPs 1 and 2 as necessary, it is considered that the requirements for the HR MSP are broadly split into 3 categories:
a) those associated with the design, establishment and embedding of a dedicated new Corporate HR Function within the boundaries of the freedoms and controls given;
b) those associated with the development, implementation and embedding of the employment policy and process framework; and
c) those associated with the DE&S workforce, including designing a HR strategy featuring a new workforce model to enable effective deployment of staff, building capability, and the delivery and embedding of a changed culture within the organisation.

Title: GB-Swindon: Water Flow Demonstration and Experimentation Facility
Description:
The Ministry of Defence has a requirement for the design, supply, and delivery to the Nuclear Department at HMS Sultan, of experimental apparatus which can be used to educate students in the fundamental principles of internal laminar and turbulent flows. Delivery should be against the technical specification defined in the Statement of Requirement.

The requirement is for a flow channel made of optically transparent material such that water flowing within the channel can be characterised using the experimental techniques of Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV), Laser Induced Fluorescence (LIF), Laser Doppler Anemometry (LDA) and Shadow Bubble Sizing. The channel should have 50 mm PN65 ASA 150 stainless steel flange connections at the top and bottom to allow for connection to the water supply and outlet pipe work. The water inlet to the channel will normally be at the bottom and the outlet at the top. The channel should be mounted in an assembly which includes a platform (in the plane normal to the direction of flow) which can be located at various vertical positions with respect to the channel. The channel should also be able to rotate around the axis parallel to the direction of flow 00 – 360o without requiring the outlet and inlet connections to be broken. The whole assembly (including the mounted channel and platform) should be mounted in a stand which allows the assembly and channel to be located in fixed positions ranging between 0o and 90o from the vertical axis.

Full details of the requirements for the Channel and Supporting Assembly are included in the tender documents.

Please note it is MOD policy to make payment via Purchase to Payment (P2P).

Title: Provision of Wireless Connectivity
Description:
The Defence School of Intelligence (DSI), part of the Ministry of Defence, is inviting solutions and costings for: 
a)	the provision of a secure connection between their Restricted Training LAN (TLAN(R)) and the Internet;
b)	rapid reconfiguration of their training environments, beginning with a small scale test environment to include User Access Devices (UADs) and other training peripherals which are capable of wireless connectivity on the TLAN(R).

The purpose of this is to rapidly reconfigure and modernise the DSI’s existing training environments to meet the current and future training requirements of the Defence Intelligence and Security Centre (JITG).

This opportunity will consist of the following:
Part 1: The provision of a connection between the Restricted Training LAN (TLAN(R)) and the Internet, to enable users to browse the Internet and download data from a Restricted terminal without compromising the integrity, confidentiality and availability of the Restricted data stored on TLAN(R).

Part 2: The provision of a small scale test environment which allows a secure wireless portal in to the TLAN(R) network whilst providing the relevant ‘back-end’ architecture to enable iterative expansion in the future. This will consists of two parts as follows:
A.	The secure wireless portal in to the TLAN(R) network
B.	The provision of a small scale test environment in two different locations, which will consist of the supply and installation of all necessary equipment to the wireless portal in each location, along with the provision of relevant IT equipment and software that allows users to access and utilise the TLAN(R) through wireless capability.

Description:
For the provision of up to 47 Ambulance Clinical Placements with NHS Ambulance Trusts. Health Education England (HEE) is mandated  by the Government to work with the MOD ‘to enhance the existing capability of the Defence Medical Service either through up-skilling of the existing workforce or by supporting the training of new entrants’.  An EMT award is considered by HEE and the DMS to be most appropriate and is achieved through an 8 week didactic course and 750 hours (20 wks) of clinical practice placements, of which not less than 15wks must be in a Pre-Hospital Emergency Care (PHEC) setting. There are no suitable military units in which to conduct the PHEC clinical practice placements, so these will have to be undertaken within Ambulance Trusts.  In order for Defence Medics to access training placements within every Ambulance Trust, they must have a level of competence acceptable to them all.  Access to ambulance placements will be achieved through a top level agreement with Health Education England and the Association of Ambulance Chief Executives (AACE) who will liaise and broker placements with the individual Ambulance Trusts across the UK

The requirement is for the provision of a Verbatim Court Recorder’s (VCR) service at all Service Court proceedings in the Court Martial, the Service Civilian Court and the Summary Appeal Court for the Army, Royal Air Force and Royal Navy (including Royal Marines). Title: GB-Glasgow: Content Audit & User Research for RAF Website Redevelopment
Description:
The Royal Air Force (RAF) has many interesting stories and persistent objectives to inform the public of the role of the RAF in protecting the UK and its interests at home & abroad. However, informing and engaging the public and internal audience is becoming increasingly difficult with the current RAF web presence. The RAF website(s) has changed little since 2006, while on other channels such as Facebook & Twitter RAF is successfully engaging users. 

Part 1 – Content Audit 
Part of the difficult facing the RAF is the size of the digital estate, there are approx 10,000 webpages across 143 sites with a corporate tone of voice, the structure & language reflecting that of the organization, rather than being user centric.
This will allow us to gain a clear understanding of the current content situation, namely the quality of the content, highlight the issues, challenges and opportunities: What content is relevant, redundant, duplicated, trivial?; What content should be kept, improved, archived? 
In an ideal situation a comprehensive evaluation qualitative and quantitative of all RAF digital content would be conducted. However, due to time & budget constraints this is not possible. Thus we propose the following approach: Automated quantitative content audit of all RAF sites; Manually qualitative content audit of a representative 10% of RAF digital content.
Part 2 – User Research 
User Needs: What do people want to know about RAF, its work / equipment etc.?; Where do people go to find the information they are looking for and can they find it?; What do they think about the information they find – is it understandable? Engaging? ; What do they do with the content once they have found it? ; How do they want to engage with the RAF & what encourages engagement? 
Structure/Info Architecture: Can the RAF web content be merged into a smaller number of sites?; How do the range of users talk about & think about the content?; Identifying the most appropriate language & content structure.
The appointed agency will be provided access to analytics, satisfaction survey results, & previous user experience research once the contract has been awarded.  This project will be focusing on gaining insight about & structuring a minimum viable product. Thus, we won’t be looking to redevelop the whole RAF digital estate in one go, with high priority/high traffic content delivered first. 
General Public Primary Audiences and MOD will undertake research activities with the internal Personnel audiences and secondary General Public audiences in parallel with the appointed agency taking responsibility for the external Primary General Public audiences.

Title: GB-Glasgow: Understanding Defence Audiences - Discovery Phase
Description:
The Ministry of Defence need to gain insight into the behaviour, needs & context of the varied audiences across the whole of UK Defence Personnel. At this stage we aim to get a baseline understanding that can be iteratively improved upon in the future.  There are approx 250,000 civilian & military personnel within Defence across geographically dispersed locations & multiple organisations as well as military personnel within Defence - regular & reserve (not just the single services &taking into consideration 2 year role rotation): 
- HOCS (Head Office and Corporate Services)
- Royal Navy
- British Army
- Royal Air Force 
- DE&S (Defence Equipment and Support)
- DIO (Defence Infrastructure Organisation)
- DSTL (Defence Science & Technology Laboratory) 
- DBS (Defence Business Services)
- JFC (Joint Force Command) 
- UKHO (UK Hydrographic Office)
- DSG (Defence Support Group) 
Within & across each organisation there are a wide variety of people in terms of experience, working environments, access to technology, needs & knowledge, behaviours. 
Insight will come from interrogating & analysing both the data MOD already has available & that gathered during this process. However, data is in different locations & will require mining from systems such as HRMS for civilians & JPA for military personnel. This suggests a very wide stakeholder community that needs to be engaged.
This project comes in the midst of a cultural shift in how technology is used, with a major overhaul & rolling out of Office 365 across Defence Personnel. Personas have been created for the New Style of IT programme which covers:
- Role activities & responsibilities  
- Mobility of personnel 
- Levels of collaboration required within roles
- Levels of use & type of information based activity
- Pain points 
- Device needs 
These elements are detailed for the following types of role that are representative within & across Defence:
- Senior Leaders  
- Line Managers
- Information Workers
- Office Enablers
- Responders 
- (Military) Trainees 
- Reservists 
- Field Workers
- (Technical) Specialists
- Contractors 
- Industrial Partners
- MOD External
- Deployed Personnel
- Personnel in Barracks  
Objectives
Gathering data from across UK Defence Personnel enhance the existing Personas covering:
- Vital statistics
- Who they are – life cycle and career cycle
- Experience & beliefs 
- General attitudes to work & Defence 
- Behaviour – what they do 
- Needs (functional, informational & emotional)
- Passion points (both positive and negative)

Title: SBRI CHALLENGE - ENHANCED INDIVIDUAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT
Description: Advances in manufacturing means that it is now becoming possible to make or modify clothing and equipment for each individual, optimising size and weight in the process. With careful design, the current set of standard sizes could be made to accommodate bespoke fittings for each user. This will allow the accurate positioning of body armour and protective headgear, helmets, masks and goggles. Using 3D printed rubber, bespoke inserts can be created quickly and cheaply to make shoes, ear and mouth protectors fit perfectly. Furthermore, the manufacturing equipment to enable this is becoming cheap and portable so that it could provide such equipment on demand and in theatre. In doing so it will improve mobility and reduce the physiological and thermal burden on the user. The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 58605 443221 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Enhanced Individual Protective Equipment Protection  programme.

Title: SBRI Challenge-Enhanced Individual Protective Equipment

The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59431-443165 part 8, as submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Enhanced Individual Protective Equipment Protection  programme.

Title: SBRI Challenge-Enhanced Individual Protective Equipment
Description:
This project will employ Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) techniques in order to produce personalised protective body armour solutions with minimum impact on the wearers performance.
Additive Manufacturing processes build parts layer-by-layer, directly from a 3D Computer-Aided Design (CAD) model, and differs from conventional manufacturing techniques as it requires no tooling. This facilitates the realisation of design concepts that are typically too expensive, difficult or impossible to create using traditional manufacturing processes, including complex internal geometries and multiple assemblies as a single unit. The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 58420-443195 part 8, as submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Enhanced Individual Protective Equipment Protection  programme.

Title: 702596452 - Alternative Navigation - Data Merging Contracts Finder Awarded Contract Notice
Description:
This Contract Award Notice is to announce the award of the 702596452 - Alternative Navigation - Data Merging contract to two suppliers, Plextek Services Limited and GMV NSL Limited.

The aim of this procurement is to award two contracts within the budgetary envelope set out in the notice. The military relies heavily on the Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), but GNSS signals are vulnerable to interference. In addition, many environments in which our military operates (inside buildings, in urban canyons, under dense foliage, underwater, and underground) have limited or no GNSS signal availability. To solve this challenge, the Alt Nav programme seeks to provide GNSS-quality PNT to military users regardless of the operational environment. This involves the merging of data within the navigation system design to prolong the availability of the PNT solution from traditional and emerging sources. The Data Merging task is the subject of this competition.

The proposed contractor(s) shall attend project management meetings to discuss information inclusive of but not limited to progress on technology development, exploitation studies, lessons learnt, details of architecture. The proposed contractor(s) shall provide a technology demonstration proving maturation of data merging technology to a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6 (TRL descriptions can be seen in additional text within this contract notice), followed by a technical report for contract completion. The project meetings, final report and demonstration will address the following themes:
Theme 1 - Preparing for near-term exploitation of Alt Nav technologies on existing MoD applications; defining and solving the engineering orientated problems of real-life examples of Data Merging and Theme 2 - Reporting lessons learned from the first task into MoD's ongoing Data Fusion Research and Development activities. In the event that Data Source contractor(s) are not able to mature the Interface Control Documentation (ICD) on time - work with the Authority to select appropriate, industry standard ICDs and data fields e.g:

- Mil GPS - GPS ICD-153 (available from the UK GNSS PO)
- Open Signal GNSS - NMEA-0183
- Inertial Measurement Unit - STANAG 4572 Open System Architecture Interface to enable simulator laboratory testing of integrated INS/GPS equipment (e.g. using SPIRENT's Sim INERTIAL simulation capability (or equivalent).
- Alt Nav Data Source - The ASPN interfaces from SET-309
- Illustrative Alt Nav Data source - based on STANAG 4278 Method of Expressing Navigation Accuracies and Draft STANAG 5645 GNSS Receiver Sensor Host ICD. 
- The MoD's emerging Assured PNT characteristics

Title: 704942450 - Modification to Lipless Firing Needle Assemblies -VTN CF
Description:
The Defence Equipment & Support Land Equipment Vehicle Support Team (VST), part of the UK Ministry of Defence, intends to award a single source contract to Rheinmetall BAE Systems Land (RBSL) ltd for the modification and supply of quantity 400 Lipless Firing needle Assembly (LFNA) for the L30A1 (120mm) gun of the Challenger 2 (CR2) main battle tank.

It is considered that this Contract can be placed on a Single Source basis with RBSL for Technical Reasons. The FNA is a safety critical internal component of the L30A1 CR2 gun that requires a key modification to the design to include a mechanical fail-safe. This modification is a safety requirement that must be fulfilled to ensure the safe functioning of the platform whilst operational.

RBSL are the Design Authority (DA) and the Original Equipment manufacturer (OEM) for the platform and therefore have all the necessary tools, skills and specialist knowledge to undertake the Firing Needle Assembly (FNA) modification to the required technical manufacturing standards.

Some CR2 platforms have recently experienced some cracking faults on the FNA which have not been seen previously; the ability to out inspect the modified FNA to the current repair specifications is paramount in the safety assurance for the LFNA.

This notice is not a request for expressions of interest so please do not apply to be invited to tender. This notice advises that the Authority has decided to negotiate a contract with the named supplier on a single source basis and is published for reasons of transparency. If you are interested in becoming a sub-contractor for this requirement, you should apply directly to the supplier named above.

The issue of this Voluntary Transparency Notice (VTN) will commence the start of a 10 day standstill period, which will end on the 2nd of October 2022 at 16:00pm, to provide opportunity to challenge this award decision.
OJEU Procedure Type: Other Single Source (non-OJEU) as value is under DSPCR 2011 Threshold

There is a requirement for specialist technical assistance to provide code assisted Vulnerability Assessments (VA) and Penetration Testing (PT) security assessments on both new and in-service applications/infrastructure.   Security assessments, PT's and VA's are used to identify vulnerabilities in code and infrastructure (networks, servers, operating systems and applications) that could potentially be exploited.   Attackers can be hackers trying to gain access into our network or systems, state sponsored activists or an insider threat.  They will aim to either extract information that is held on applications and hosting environments or cause extensive disruption to services. 

ADS has 2 hosting environments, the Army Hosting Environment (AHE) and Joint Server Farm (JSF). The JSF is accessible from the internet via the Defence Gateway and holds information classified at Official. The AHE holds Official, Secret and Sensitive Personal Information which if extracted would not only be damaging to the Army's reputation, it could jeopardise potential operations. It could also incur fines from the Information Commissioner if there were a breach of personal information.  An attack to disrupt any of the services ADS provides would significantly erode the Army's ability to operate, as many of the systems support day to day activities and processes. It is therefore imperative that vulnerabilities are identified and remedied/mitigated to reduce the risk of these occurrences. 

All new applications expecting to be hosted on the AHE or the JSF must have a vulnerability assessment before being allowed onto the environment to ensure there are no weaknesses which could potentially allow an attacker access to the wider infrastructure and applications.  Existing applications, hosting environments and platforms must be VA'd on a rolling programme to ensure any changes do not increase vulnerability and potential for being attacked.

Title: 704030450 - TRANSPARENCY NOTICE
Description:
The UK Ministry of Defence has awarded a contract to BAE Systems (Operations) Limited for the estimated value of £1,639,000 ex VAT for the support for the Hawk TMk2A Release to Service. pursuant to the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011 (DSPCR 2011) using the negotiated procedure without prior publication of a contract notice. In accordance with regulation 4 of The Defence and Security Public Contracts (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/697) this procurement falls to be regulated under the provisions of the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011 as amended (in particular by SI 2019/697 and SI 2020/1450). It is considered that the award of the contract without prior publication of a contract notice in the UK e-notification service (as required by the relevant legislation) is lawful in accordance with regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the DSPCR 2011.

UK RAF QFIs and pilots are due to fly on the Qatari owned Hawk MK 167 aircraft on the Joint Hawk Training Squadron currently being stood up at RAF Leeming. Currently, this Hawk TMk2A variant aircraft does not have certification from the Military Aviation Authority (MMA) to operate safely in UK airspace. The UK MOD and 11 Sqn Qatar Emiri Air Force (QEAF) have a critical dependency on the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the Hawk TMk2A BAE Systems, to certify the aircraft, when operated in accordance with the Release to Service Recommendation (RTSR), is airworthy and safe in all respects.

This procedure is considered justified for technical reasons under regulation 16 (1)(a)(ii) of the DSPCR 2011. In order to award a UK RTS, there must be adequate evidence artefacts provided by the OEM and accepted by the MAA and Release to Service Authority (RTSA) to support the airworthiness statements. BAES are the OEM and single supplier with the required detailed technical understanding of the aircraft and possession of the technical documentation for the required evidence. The award of this contract allows UK MOD personnel to operate the aircraft under a UK MOD governance framework.

Title: DInfoCom/0174 - Provision of Exploitation of Tactical Data Links within Land Information Manoeuvre
Description:
The Land Environment Tactical Communications and Information Systems (LE TacCIS) programme aims to deliver tactical military communications and consists of multiple projects delivering elements of an intended single network.  The LE TacCIS Innovation, Research Experimentation (IRE) activities aims to conduct programme level research and experimentation to de-risk solution development for a wider Land Domain Communication and Information System (LD CIS) perspective and consider what areas require development to ensure that individual projects remain able to deliver their elements of the Single Information Environment. 

The intent of the LE TacCIS-IRE activities includes technical de-risking of programme themes and addressing themes that cover multiple projects and provides a means of including innovative thought into LE TacCIS.  This activity will support the Networks theme of the IRE activities and in particular Tactical Data Links (TDL). 

Tactical Information exchange has never needed to be more accurate, agile and timely to keep pace with persistent and high tempo changes across the battlespace.  To achieve an efficient and effective tactical outcome in national and international environments, the automated and secure exchange of (near) real-time Situational Awareness, Battlespace Management and Command and Control functions can be fulfilled by Tactical Data Links.  Several varieties of TDLs have been developed, each designed to support a difference domain and/or warfare demand. 

Building on the outputs of Phase 1 TDL study conducted in 2021 (DInfoCom/0125), deliver a more detailed technical study on the technicalities and practical implementation of a TDL network architecture within the Land Domain that can complement current and future LE TacCIS and Land ISTAR capabilities (and other multi domain links).

Title: Participation in an Innovative Partnership for mTBI -Predict: Baseline Variability Study (Mild Traumatic Brain Injury)
Description:
Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI - otherwise known as concussion) is common in UK civilian practice and was one of the "signature injuries" of Operation HERRICK - affecting almost 1:10 of those deployed in combat roles. Although termed "mild" this type of injury frequently leads to a disproportionate impact on future health with almost one third of those affected unable to work at 12 months - usually as a result of ongoing symptoms including persistent headaches, imbalance, memory disturbance, and poor mental health.

The UK TBI is a consortium of top expert opinion, led by the University of Birmingham.  It includes acclaimed academics in the field of mTBI from Imperial College London, University of Nottingham, University Hospitals Coventry & Warwickshire and the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre, alongside those from the University of Birmingham and University Hospitals Birmingham.

 The consortium has devised and written an extensive protocol for the mTBI-Predict trial which will assess the accuracy, reproducibility and practicality of a variety of biomarkers including brain imaging, Magnetoencephalography (MEG), cerebral physiology, markers in blood and saliva, headache, mental health, vision, balance, and cognitive performance in a long-term cohort study following 800 patients for 24 months after a new mTBI.
