Title: Provision of Actors for Role Play to Support the Training of Visiting Officers
Description:
The Bereavement and Aftercare Support (BAS) Team is located in Ramillies Building, Marlborough Lines, Andover, and is responsible for the training of Visiting Officers (VO), whose job is to support Army bereaved families.  BAS plans between 15 and 20 courses each year, with ten held at the Armed Forces Chaplaincy Centre (AFCC), Beckett House, in the Defence Academy at Shrivenham near Swindon in Wiltshire, with the remainder run in the more distant Garrisons as required, such as Northern Ireland, Scotland, South Wales, Preston, Colchester, Hereford, Catterick  and Cyprus.  Courses cater for a maximum of 35 students, drawn from regular and reserve Army units, and last for three days, with the third day being devoted to Role Play with professional actors. The role play is based on five syndicates of seven students each, and uses 20 pre-written scenarios, issued by the Authority, spread between three female and two male actors on each course of 35 students - this requirement will vary if there are fewer students on the course as explained in Para 5 below. Each student conducts one role play of 15-20 minutes, followed by 15-20 minutes critique and discussion, which includes feed-back from the actor.     

 

Scope: 

The actors must appreciate that they are taking part in the training of professional soldiers, many with long service and operational experience, and that the role-play is not there to test them.  When in character, they must portray the full emotions of the bereaved person within the scenario setting, and should be alert to the strengths and weaknesses of the student, responding accordingly so as not to break them.   They must appreciate that any nerves or diffidence, demonstrated by the student, are quite likely to be replaced by compassion and general confidence when away from the unreality of a syndicate role-play setting.  The actors are also expected to show an awareness of the military environment, and an understanding of the aim of the training, to enable visiting officers to provide support to the bereaved, and not to act as counsellors, for which a separate background brief is available.

Notice Identifier: Counter Improvised Explosive Device (C-IED) Training and Assurance Application
Title: Contract Awarded: Counter Improvised Explosive Device (C-IED) Training and Assurance Application on Digital Skills and Outcomes
Description:
MOD require an app developer to create an app to support the training and assurance of service persons using ground search detectors in a counter improvised explosive device (C-IED) role.

There is currently no ability to provide quantitative feedback on the use of ground search detectors to the users and their commanders. The ability to correctly use a detector is critical in ensuring the threats are detected. Data to enable an understanding of how a detector is being swung in three dimensions (relative to the ground) and where the user is located in relation to the rest of the team is not currently available. The user and their commander will need feedback from the application to enable training and assurance.

A training detector is being developed to solve this problem and generate the data required using commercial sensors and hardware. An application is required to support the sensors and hardware in generating the quantitative data and feedback. The users and their commanders will be able to access a visual representation of the data collected by the sensors via an app to enhance both training and assurance processes.

Award documentation being published for transparency purposes only.

Title: GB-Glasgow: JFC6C/00031 Exercise Prescription Licences
Description:
Exercise prescription is a core element of rehabilitation of injuries in Defence.  Exercise description, frequency and progression must be clearly documented by the clinician in order to provide a comprehensive medical record and to act as a reference document for the patient to ensure the delivery of a safe and effective individual exercise programme. A hosted software solution is required which enables the production and digital sharing of bespoke individual exercise programmes. 
      
      The Contractor is to provide a hosted software solution which:
      •	Allows the production of bespoke, individual exercise programmes .
      •	Has a broad ranging catalogue of exercises relevant to the physical rehabilitation of musculoskeletal injury, neurological injury and disease.
      •	Produces exercise sheets with clear pictorial reference which has an editable written description (allowing modification of elements such as resistance, frequency and number of repetitions).
      •	Produces templates, which can be shared with other users, for common individual exercise programmes .
      •	Is capable of supporting a variety of media.
      •	Produces exercise prescriptions which can be published and shared with the patient via digital transmission and produce a record which can be stored in the e-health record (eHR). Once published the record must be non-modifiable.
      •	Has a unique login for each authorised clinician. 
      
      
      A web based portal is required, which is accessible from any worldwide web terminal. The exercise prescription output must comply with the Healthcare Professions Council (HCPC) standard for medical documentation (physiotherapy standards). In addition the portal must allow the development of additional Authority exercise programmes for specialist areas such as catered for at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine.
      
      The evaluation criterion for this requirement is Most Economically Advantageous to Tender (MEAT) with an agreed scoring weighting of 60 Technical and 40 Price. 
      
      Should you have any questions please contact Aileen McLynn, Commercial Manager on DefComrclCC-JFC6a@mod.uk.

The 3SST2015 is a strategically important programme for STFC RAL Space and UK (via UK Space Agency and UK Ministry of Defence) with key milestones which must be met if UK is to achieve its objectives and deliver its commitments in this international programme. The 3SST2015 is part of the SST-Framework which will continue until 2020 when it will be succeeded by the SST-Programme. The aim of this tender is to contribute to the EU SST WPs 4-6 in order to enable STFC ( a sub-contractor to UKSA, the UK Beneficiary to the H2020 grant which makes STFC a Third Party subcontractor in the EU's H2020 framework) to fulfil their commitments to UKSA. The services and support provided by STFC for the 3SST2015 contract will be managed as projects within RAL Space's standard processes and structures. The project will be supported by the RAL Space Business and Finance Management Teams and by the STFC Legal and Commercial Team. The RAL Space Director is ultimately responsible for the delivery of the project on specification, schedule and budget. Work Package 4; Support WP4 weekly telecoms, if required. Work Package 5; generate an internal deliverable summarising UK SST priorities; Deliver (see the list of Deliverables under the Timetable section below); D5.2 Report of R&D Plan and studies for sensors and operations; D5.3 Final action Plan (including scopes, roadmap and priorities); D5.4 yearly funding planning. All work packages; Generate inputs to UKSA 3SST2015 project reports to facilitate their project reporting activities after the project end.  RAL Space PM will request the specific inputs one month prior to the project end on 31/12/2017.Travel may be required throughout this requirement and will be in line with STFC's travel and Substance policy and all travel must be approved by the authorising manager within STFC. Title: Repair of a Quantity not to exceed 100 of the X200 Transmissions for the Bulldog Armoured Fighting Vehicle Platform
Description:
Babcock acting as the Authority's Agent, intend to negotiate a single source enabling contract with Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd, for the repair of a quantity to not exceed 100 of the X200 Transmissions fitted to the Bulldog Armoured Fighting Vehicle Platform. 

It is considered that this Contract can be placed using the Negotiated procedure without prior publication pursuant to Article 28(1)(e) of the Directive 2009/81/EC(Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the UK Defence and Security Public Contract Regulations 2011) for technical reasons. 

Allison Transmissions are the OEM, all drawings and specifications of the X200 were developed with internal funding and are proprietary to them, and are a highly specialised type of transmission modified to fit the specific application. This requirement is for the repair and reconditioning of the X200. Without the detailed technical information referenced above a Supplier would not be able to ensure repaired and reconditioned X200's were fit for purpose in accordance with the original design specifications, or maintain configuration control such as build standards, drawing and test specifications. The X200 is part of the safety critical part of the Bulldog powertrain and is therefore essential to the safe operation of the Bulldog platforms and maintaining the status of the safety case at ALARP. 

Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd are the only agent in the UK that Allison licence to carry out work on their range of defence products and as a consequence Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd is the only supplier with access to the design information and technical details, data and knowledge necessary to fulfil the requirement. The design information and technical details, data and knowledge are not available to any other supplier. 

This notice is not a request for expressions of interest so please do not apply to be invited to tender. This notice advises that the UK Ministry of Defence is to place a single source non-qualifying contract with the named supplier to satisfy repairs to critical assets whilst an enduring solution is progressed.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DIO, Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO)
Title: Oil Fuel Depot Gosport, Tank Farm Project
Description:
The Oil Fuel Depot (OFD) Gosport has been operational for more than 100 years and some of the current operational infrastructure was constructed before World War One. All tanks are of rivited plate steel construction. This type of tank construction ceased in the commercial sector in the 1960's.The existing tanks have undergone packages of maintenance works to extend their out of service dates as agreed with the competent authority, the Health and Safety Executive. 
      The requirement is to raze and rebuild the tanks and associated infrastructure at the Oil Fuel Depot in Gosport whilst keeping the site open and maintaining operational capability for the customer. To achieve this requirement the works will need to be completed in a phased delivery approach, bringing new tanks online to align with the existing tank "out of service" dates in order to maintain the fuel holding requirements. 
      The Contractor will be responsible for all activities associated with the raze and rebuild element, including but not limited to demolition and targeted remediation activities on the new Tank Farm footprint. The new tank farm scope will include but is not limited to:
      •	Fuel Storage Tanks - Envisaged 6 primary storage tanks with 5 smaller supporting tanks.
      •	Bunding in accordance with current operational standards.
      •	Associated pipework
      •	Fuel delivery systems including pump sets
      •	Admin / control room
      •	Security elements in line with MOD Standards.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DSTL, Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (DSTL)
Title: R-Cloud Framework Renewal
Description:
The Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl), which is part of the UK Ministry of Defence, wishes to renew it's commercial framework for Science and Technology (S&T) research contracts, known as R-Cloud (Research Cloud). Dstl places extensive fundamental, experimental and applied research with industry and academic suppliers and wants to broaden access for this supply base, reducing the cost of trading with Dstl and enabling agile contracting. R-Cloud complements Dstl's other contracting mechanisms and academic and industry suppliers of S&T research will be invited to pre-qualify onto it to join Dstl's research supplier community. The ownership of any intellectual property generated will remain with the suppliers. Although this requirement is exempt from the Procurement Regulations as it is for Research activities, Dstl is advertising and competing for new participants. For existing R-Cloud suppliers further information and guidance about this renewal process will be published on the R-Cloud portal https://rcloud.dstl.gov.uk/ . New suppliers interested in registering for R-Cloud should apply by  e-mail to dstlrcloud@dstl.gov.uk , giving their name, address and contact details and will then be contacted to be included in the renewal process.
      
      This call relates to a series of R-Cloud frameworks covering eight Capability Areas as follows: 
      •	Command, Control, Communication & Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR)
      •	Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN)
      •	Counter Terrorism and Security (CT&S)
      •	Cyber
      •	Human Capability (HC)    
      •	Integrated Survivability (IS)
      •	Platform Systems (PS)
      •	Weapons
      
      R-Cloud provides a low barrier to entry for potential suppliers and offers direct access to Dstl's current and future research requirements. Academic and industrial suppliers of research are invited to pre-qualify onto the R-Cloud framework. A standard form of contract has been drawn up which details the terms and conditions for entry onto the R-Cloud framework. Acceptance of these terms and conditions is mandatory.

Title: LSBU15/0133 - The Calibration and Repair of Test and Measurement Equipment used across the MoD Tri-Service community
Description:
Babcock DSG Limited acting as the UK Ministry of Defence's Agent seeks to place a Multiple Supplier Framework Agreement for the Calibration and Repair of Test Equipment used across the MoD Tri-Service community, for the duration of two years with the potential to extend for a further 2 years.

      The services within the scope of this Framework Agreement have been divided into 28 lots, covering 'Calibration' and 'Calibration and Repair', for both Electrical and Mechanical items in line with UKAS categorisation.  Suppliers who progress to the Invitation to Tender Stage can bid for one lot, several lots or combination of lots. A framework agreement covering all lots or framework agreements for individual or combination of lots will be awarded based upon the best price and technical capability for all lots over the 4 year contract period.
      
      QA Standards or equivalent: The service provider shall hold and maintain a certification to BS EN ISO 9001:2008, issued by an accredited certification body, and must stipulate that each calibration facility is a BS EN 17025 accredited Laboratory. Title: WO0268 Ludgershall Perham Primary School
Description:
Following an Army Basing Review undertaken by the Ministry of Defence (MOD) in March 2003, it has been decided by the MOD that the Brigade Headquarters of the British Army Reaction Force is to be relocated to the Salisbury Plain Training Area with three Armoured Infantry Brigades. 

As a consequence, an additional 4,000 military personnel and their families will be relocated to Tidworth, Ludgershall, Bulford and Larkhill. This process has already started and is due to be completed in circa 2019.

A major implication of this Army re-basing programme is that additional facilities such as Schools, Housing, Leisure Facilities, Health and Social Services need to be provided to meet the increase in population in the affected areas.

Within the Ludgershall area, it has been identified that there is a need for the development of a new two form entry primary school including a thirty-place nursery to be located on a circa 2.3-hectare parcel of land provided by the MOD via a Section 106 Agreement within the site of the former Corruna Barracks in Ludgershall. The requirement is that the new school and nursery is operationally ready to accept pupils by September 2019 which is the purpose of this tender opportunity.

________________________________

The original Contract Notice was published in the OJEU on the following link:

The Workshop Tools & Equipment (WTE) team are part of the Support & Test Equipment (STE) area in Operational Infrastructure (OI) and are responsible for the through life management of workshop tools and equipment. The Core Contract duration is 2 years (until 30/9/2020), with 2 1-year Options. For purposes of the Contract Award Notice, the full 4 years has been stated as the duration.

Title: GB-Bristol: Data Collection Tool for AWE18
Description:
EXPERIMENTATION DATA CAPTURE OVERVIEW OF USER FOR ARMY WARFIGHTING EXPERIMENT 2018
      The Army Warfighting Experiment 2018 (AWE18), Autonomous Warrior (Land) (AW(L) is the Army's premier experimentation activity for 2018, taking place in and around Salisbury Plain between 12 November 2018 and 12 December 2018. 
      A stand-alone system, deployed to personnel through portable handheld devices, is required to assist in the planning, designing, conducting, collecting and reporting of information gathered during AWE18. The requirements of the system are:
      -	the ability to have specific experiment design/data loaded prior to the experiment commencement date.
      -	to capture and collate real time multimedia data from a variety of sources such as photo, video and text. 
      -	to collect time and location specific information against pre-set criteria, for a variety of different equipment. 
      -	to take information gathered to produce reports in a variety of standard text formats on equipment performance. 
      -	to be able to produce evidence (based on inputs) to enable the evaluation of performance against pre-set criteria of individual and groups of equipment during the experiment. 
      -	to withstand potential adverse weather conditions. 
      -	to permit data collected during experimentation to be shared between users and extracted and stored by the user.
      -	to be a secure system for the users access only for the duration of the contract
      -	no experimentation data collected by the user will be held by the contractor at the end of the experimental period.
      -	50 portable hand held devices will be required from between 1st November 2018 and 31st December 2018.  
      -	provision of train-the-trainer for 5 'super-users' for the systems will be required prior to the experiment commencement date.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, ISTAR, Situational Awareness Command and Control (SACC) Delivery Team
Title: Provision of Technical Support to the UK Link 16 Frequency Clearance Agreement
Description:
The Situational Awareness Command and Control Deliver Team, (SACC DT), part of the UK Ministry of Defence (MoD), intends to award a new Contract for the support, repair, maintenance and storage of the Frequency Clearance (FC) System. This Contract will be for an initial period of 24 (24) months with two (2) twelve (12) month extension options.   
      The principal requirements of the Link 16 Frequency Clearance Support contract are as follows:
      •	To undertake compatibility testing of Link 16 with Communications Navigation and Surveillance (CNS) systems operating in the 960-1215MHz frequency band, using the government furnished FC Test equipment, known as the 8 Net Signal Source. This is a collection of bespoke test equipment enabling interference testing of Link 16 on civilian aeronautical CNS equipment, as required by the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) under the terms of the FC Agreement (FCA). 
      •	To support of all aspects of Link 16 network management, monitoring, design, planning and the technical aspects of the FCA to support the Joint Data Link Management Organisation (JDLMO), including working with the JDLMO to maintain compliance with the terms of the FCA, including the CAA audit process, and maintaining clearance to radiate for all Link 16 platforms in the UK Flight Information Region. 
      •	To manage and maintain the Link 16 FCA Safety Management System (FCA SMS) and all associated documentation on behalf of the MoD and CAA. The FCA SMS includes the Safety and Environmental Management Plan, Baseline Safety Case, Terminal Safety Cases (Generic and Specific variants) and Platform Safety Cases. A Subject Matter Expert is required to manage the FCA SMS including technically reviewing Terminal and Platform Safety Cases and staffing them though the FCA Safety Committee approvals process. A detailed knowledge of the background and content of the above documents is required to deliver this requirement.  
      •	In order to deliver this requirement a detailed knowledge of how Link 16 interferes with CNS systems, and the ability to undertake interference assessments against the following equipment is required: Distance Measuring Equipment (DME), Tactical Air Navigation Aids (TACAN), Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR), Automatic Dependent Surveillance (Broadcast) ADS-B, 1090 MHz Multilateration, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and L-Band Digital Aeronautical Communications (L-DAC

Support. This contract provides in-service support to a fleet of thirty-five workboats operated by the United Kingdom (UK) Ministry of Defence (MOD). These boats range from 11 metres to 18 metres in length and their modular design allows them to support various users based in both domestic and overseas locations.
Accelerated Justification:
The Accelerated Restricted Procedure was used on this occasion to ensure operational outputs would still be achieved. These outputs include provision of training, including to new joiners to the Royal Navy; diving operations; and inshore survey operations. Inability to provide proactive and reactive maintenance to the vessels providing these outputs, which would have occurred by not using this
procedure, would have resulted in rapid withdrawal from service and therefore to follow the usual time limits would have had a genuine adverse effect on our ability to maintain operational outputs. In order to ensure the prospective contract was only bound to the essential scope urgently required, the contract was to be let for a period of two years, with a view that longer term support to this fleet would be factored into a future competitive procurement to be let by 31 Mar 26.

Title: JSENS/00188 Synergia Contract 4 VTN
Description:
The issue of this Voluntary Transparency Notice (VTN) will commence the start of a 10 day standstill period, which will end on the 30th of June 2024 at 09:00am, to provide opportunity to challenge this award decision.

The Joint Sensors and Engagement Networks Team, part of the UK Ministry of Defence ("the Authority"), intends to award a contract for a period of three years with two option years costed and one option year uncosted (total contract term six years) to Leonardo UK LTD ("Leonardo") for the continued in-service support and provision of software licences for the Counter Uncrewed Air System (C-UAS) Orcus System. The total estimated value of the contract is £40,000,000 (Ex VAT).

The Authority considers that the award of this proposed contract can be made directly to Leonardo because competition is absent for technical reasons.

Leonardo is the Original Equipment Manufacturer and Design Authority for the integrated C-UAS Orcus system and the only supplier with the required technology to provide a C-UAS system that meets the Authority's specific requirements. This is in part due to the algorithms and other software that are proprietary to Leonardo and in which they have Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) resulting from significant Private Venture investment prior to the start of the C-UAS project. As such, Leonardo holds the knowledge and expertise of the Authority's current fielded in-service Orcus capability and developmental history of the system over its lifetime. 

Consequently, only Leonardo have the necessary technical knowledge and expertise, design data and technical documentation, executive files, and software source code to carry out the required in-service support. Further, only Leonardo can provide the necessary software licences needed in order to deliver the Authority's requirements and maintain the current Orcus capability.


Further details can be found within the project Opportunity Listing in the Defence Sourcing Portal (DSP) at https://contracts.mod.uk/esop/guest/go/opportunity/detail?opportunityId=58322

Title: Foxhound Technical Demonstrator
Description:
*VOLUNTARY TRANSPARENCY NOTICE ONLY*

Army Commercial, part of the United Kingdom Ministry of Defence (MoD), intends to award a twenty-four-month contract to General Dynamics United Kingdom Limited to produce up to three Foxhound (FHD) vehicle Technical Demonstrator Platforms (TDP) and associated technical publications.  The content of these publications includes but are not limited to, information on manufacture, support, upgrade, trials, test and evaluation. 

The TDPs will be used by the MoD to assess whether the current in-service FHD fleet could be modified to extend its use beyond the current Out of Service Date (2030).    There is a Future Soldier FHD Land Fleet Requirement deficit and the TDPs will allow the MoD to understand whether new build FHDs could meet the extant FHD requirement.  Furthermore, the TDPs will also be used to ascertain the suitability of the FHD as a vehicle that may be procured to replenish other military vehicles that were Gifted in Kind to Ukraine.  
In accordance with regulation 4 of The Defence and Security Public Contracts (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/697) this procurement falls to be regulated under the provisions of the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011 as amended (in particular by SI 2019/697 and SI 2020/1450). Prior publication of a contract notice in the Official Journal of the European Union is no longer appropriate.

It is considered that this contract can be placed using the Negotiated Procedure Without Prior Publication of a Contract Notice in the UK e-notification service (in accordance with the relevant legislation) pursuant to Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the DSPCR 2011 (as amended) for Technical Reasons.

This is because General Dynamics UK Ltd are the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Design Authority for the FHD platform, which has been in-service with the MoD since 2012 and supported by this supplier since then.  As the OEM they are the only supplier with the necessary technical data and required skills and experience to build FHD TDPs. 

It is our intention to award a contract in late 2024 for a period of 24 months. 

This notice is not a request for expressions of interest so please do not apply to be invited to tender. This notice advises that the Authority has decided to negotiate a contract with the named supplier on a single source basis, and is published for reasons of transparency. If you are interested in becoming a sub-contractor for this requirement, you should apply directly to the supplier named above.

A Voluntary Transparency Notice has been submitted to Find a Tender via the DSP.

Title: DSRS Site 1 Uplift Works
Description:
The Defence Strategic Radio Service (DSRS) provides long-range radio communica-tions for MOD and UK Government and will deliver safe, robust and effective High Frequency (HF) Services.

The current infrastructure does not provide the accreditation required and therefore needs to be uplifted accordingly. These Uplift works will allow DSRS to achieve the new acceptable accreditation.

The project will be completed in multiple phases and the 'Phase One' (Design) deliverables will be for a feasibility study and submission of a firm price for the design to build and deliver the overall project requirements. 

Specific Requirements for Phase One includes:

•	Co-ordination of an initial requirements meeting with the client and stake-holders
•	Surveys to confirm current systems capabilities.
•	An integrated schedule for the design & build phase.

Title: MSKI-Prevent
Description:
This is a requirement for a research program to identify individual level risk predictions of musculoskeletal injury (MSKI) and training outcome and the impact of injury prevention interventions. A recent review of MSKIs across HQ Army Recruiting and Initial Training

Command (ARITC) training units has identified high levels of MSKIs in the recruit population, including a recent rise in MSKI prevalence, impacting on the training pipeline.

Musculoskeletal injuries (MSKIs) continue to represent a major cause of lost training days, re-squadding and medical discharge (MD) during training. This program will support MSKI reduction both within the trainee population and wider Army and contribute to Future Soldier and the Army Plan.

A combination of wearable technology, physical assessments, and subjective measures will be utilised to acquire data on potential predictors with a focus on modifiable risk factors.

Title: RECODE - In Service Support for Combat Management Systems (CMS), Shared Infrastructure (SI) and Networks - Contract Awarded
Description:
This is a notice to inform the market that the Surface Ships Combat Systems Group Delivery Team which is part of the United Kingdom Ministry of Defence has placed a contract with BAE Systems Surface Ships Ltd (BAES) for In Service Support of Combat Management Systems (CMS), BAES Shared Infrastructure (SI) & Networks for Royal Navy platforms, Land-Based Test Sites & training sites as well as the installation of SI Version 3 on Type 45 Destroyers. The platforms in scope include Type 23 Frigates, T45, Queen Elizabeth Class Aircraft Carrier, Landing Platform Dock, Royal Fleet Auxiliary, Type 26 Frigates & support for the hosting infrastructure on the Type 31 Frigates to enable the hosting of the Maritime Electronic Warfare Systems Integrated Capability (MEWSIC). 

A CMS is a multi-layered system, comprising of component parts, products & individual equipment which all work together to provide situational awareness & lethality to the operator. The CMS covers: CMS Software & Hardware, and Hosting Infrastructure through SI & Combat System Networks. CMS equipment is made up of a series of discrete sub-systems, fully integrated together to provide the interface from which Operators can achieve a platform's Decide & Enable capabilities. Integration & configuration management is performed at the system level to ensure interoperability across the respective sub-systems.

Title: Delivery of Operational Safety Cases For HMNB Clyde
Description:
The Government White Paper published in December 2006 set out the United Kingdom (UK) Government's intention to retain a minimum assured independent strategic nuclear deterrent for the foreseeable future. This will be fulfilled by the Dreadnought SSBN as the replacement for the V-Class.

Operationally, the Dreadnought Nuclear Powered Warship (NPW) will provide the 'replacement' capability for the V-Class NPW rather than providing a 'new' capability. Consequently, the expected mission and functional requirements can be assumed to be essentially the same as those of the V-Class NPW. However, the reactor design in Dreadnought is Pressurised Water Reactor (PWR) 3 as opposed to PWR2 in V-Class - the change in design of the reactor and its associated systems means that Safety Justifications (SJs) for Dreadnought operations at HMNB(C) may place different requirements to V-Class.

Consequently, there is a requirement to establish, and maintain across the project timeframe, a suitably qualified and experienced technical team and deliver a suite of Operational Safety Cases (OSCs) for His Majesty's Naval Base (Clyde) (HMNB(C)) to Relevant Good Practice (RGP) and within the timescales imposed by the HMNB(C) Dreadnought Readiness Date.

The suite of OSCs will justify NPW activities undertaken at the HMNB(C) Authorised Site, initially to justify Dreadnought activities and enable HMNB(C) to meet the Dreadnought Readiness Date, and ultimately to update the OSCs to justify Astute and Vanguard Class activities so that the HMNB(C) safety cases for all NPW activities meet RGP.

Title: Provision of Policing Skills Support to the Iraq Historic Allegations Team (IHAT)
Description:
The MOD has a requirement for an investigative capability to work in support of the Royal Navy Police (RNP) within the Iraq Historic Allegations Team (IHAT). The IHAT is based in Upavon, Wiltshire.  It is responsible for the investigation of allegations arising from British military operations in Iraq between 2003 and 2009.  It operates within the statutory framework of the Armed Forces Act 2006 and all investigative activity is carried out under the day to day supervision and control of the Director IHAT and the Senior RNP Officer.
The contractor must be able to provide a large number (circa 127) of suitably qualified and experienced personnel to support the RNP across a range of specialist policing functions and roles.  Their tasks will include: the interviewing of witnesses, casework research and analysis, the running of a Major Incident Room and carrying out forensic analysis.  Some of the contractor's personnel will also be required to fill management roles within IHAT and to assist in the development of investigative strategies.

Description:
The Artillery Systems Team, part of the UK Ministry of Defence (“MOD”), intends to award SAAB AB the Mobile Artillery Monitoring Battlefield Radar (MAMBA) Mid Life Extension (MLE) Contract commencing  April 2018 addressing end of life equipment/components via technical re-design and re-configuring the Radar equipment within a standardized 12ft container so that the system is vehicle agnostic, this includes obsolescence rectification, equipment modification/re-design, post MLE includes  obsolescence management, maintenance, repair and configuration management of the  Mobile Artillery Monitoring Battlefield Radar (MAMBA) MLE for a total period of 8 years which includes 5 years in-service support . It is considered that this contract can be placed using the negotiated procedure without prior publication as permitted by Article 28(1)(e) of Directive 2009/81/EC (Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011) for technical reasons because only SAAB AB have the specific technological expertise and knowledge , tools and specialist test equipment to carry out the modification work to deliver the required outputs of the MLE project. 

The MAMBA system is a Weapon Locating Radar (WLR) designed, developed and supported soley by SAAB AB.  Only SAAB AB have the necessary and specific technological skills and knowledge of MAMBA to be able to provide the re-design and obsolescence support services required by the MOD to deliver the required outputs of the MLE project through-life. As the Design Authority (DA), SAAB AB have ownership of essential drawings, designs, and associated technical data.  They have the underlying knowledge, skills and expertise, particularly in the area of ballistic algorithms, required for design and modification elements of the contract. SAAB AB are the only company that has the  detailed understanding of the design of MAMBA. 

SAAB AB are the only company that can combine technical re-design with maintenance and repair activities with the requirement for supporting the equipment through-life. Current Out of Service Date is 2016 including obsolescence management and solutions.  No other party has the necessary technical expertise and knowledge required to modify the equipment as the modifications cannot be undertaken without access to proprietary design information.     
As the contracted DA, any modifications developed by a third party would have to be underwritten by SAAB AB resulting in disproportionate technical and safety difficulties for the MOD along with a disproportionate impact on time and cost in order to provide MOD with the necessary assurances the system safety and performance had not been compromised.

Title: GB-Swindon: Design, Supply and Delivery of a Chemistry and Materials High Pressure and High Temperature (HP/HT) Dynamic Flow Rig.
Description:
1.	The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply and delivery to the Nuclear Department at HMS Sultan, of experimental apparatus which is to be used to examine the performance characteristics of a number of candidate test materials in the presence of flowing high temperature and pressure aqueous fluids. To include a minimum 1 year warranty, costings for subsequent annual safety assessments, ½ day familiarisation training (to be delivered within 3 weeks of receipt), taking test equipment up to full pressure and temperature conditions and an operating manual. It will be important for the test column to be readily removed from the test rig and be amenable to easy discharge and subsequent re-filling with test material prior to use again. Test conditions up to 200 bar and 300°C are required.

3.	The MoD will require a “rough” Computer Aided Design (CAD) drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to display full rig assembly and functionality.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, Ships, Communications and Situational Awareness (CSA)
Title: Navigation Radar Portfolio Project
Description:
The Navigation Radar Portfolio (NRP) is a capability sustainment project that will replace the current Navigation Radars on the Ships and Submarines of the Fleet.  The scope of this programme is Primary Navigation Radars (I Band), Second Navigation Radars (E/F Band) and Compact I Band Radars.  Although the NRP is capability sustainment and funded through the Equipment Support Programme (ESP), there are new and enhanced regulations that form part of the requirement.  These are IMO regulations and the MAA regulations, the latter being supported by Def Stan 00-972.  The MAA regulations have to be adhered to due to the Primary Navigation Radar utilisation for Helicopter management.  The NRP also has a ‘UK Eyes Only’ requirement embedded in the Radar requirements.  It is envisaged that radar installation will commence in 2016 and be completed by 2020 and the capability will remain extant for 20 years from installation.

There is a further NRP requirement to provide as much convergence of capability across the Fleet and to reduce Defence Lines of Development (DLoD) expenditure.  This is a key driver in the maritime domain.  The NRP project seeks to ensure as much commonality in spares, HMI and operator/maintainer experience between the I Band and the E/F Band radars.  Additionally, the NRP has to consider the use of the bandwidth, in particular the likely event of spectrum sell-off, particularly in the E/F band.

Title: TRANSPARENCY ONLY-DOCUMENTS PROVIDED FOR TRANSPARENCY ONLY IN RELATION TO: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)
Description: NOTE: This notice was updated on 10 February 2016 for the following reason: Change to EOI deadline to fit with business needs.1. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department. 2. The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety. As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3. 3. The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered. 4. It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system. The new system should allow for a short, timed, interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data). In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area. Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students). 5. The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality. 6. The Authority envisages a need for a brief site survey to enable potential suppliers to inspect the facility and compile accurate measurements of the installation site. This is planned to take place on 15 Feb 16 13:30. 7. The Authority has the desire for delivery and installation by the end of Mar 2016 Full details of the requirements for the Supply, Delivery and Installation of Safety Equipment for a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) will be included in the tender documents. Title: SBRI Challenge - Non Destructive Evaluation (NDE)
Description:
Develop a highly sensitive vapour detector based on an already existing technology, that can be used to assess the state of hydraulic seals and to detect fuel and hydraulic fluid leaks. The device will be able to detect trace levels of vapours (part per billion) and offer a more precise and accurate way of detecting fuel and hydraulic fluid leaks. It would also help to locate a damaged seal that is about to cause a leak. The device will provide instantaneous reading of the detected level of the targeted vapour and will be portable and easily deployable. It will operate on a 'switch on and detect' basis, with little to no maintenance and no consumables needed, therefore will be very easy to maintain in working condition. Because the sensor is based on laser technology, it shall be safe to the human eye.
 Identify the spectroscopic requirements of the analyser (e.g. review the fluids / fuel composition,Identify the target compounds,
 Perform spectroscopic absorption preliminary measurements, select the lasers,
 Assess the stability of vapours of fuel
 Modify a laboratory-based analyser and integrate the lasers,
 Complete a demonstration proof-of-concept of the prototype and
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59529-446169 submitted and held by Innovate UK for the Non-Destructive Evaluation programme. Key Deliverables are:
1. Intermediate Report: results and conclusions of Phase 1a (01/02/2016)
2. Develop and demonstrate a working prototype of the proposed system (02/05/2016)
3. Delivery of Final Report of all Phase 1 activities and findings (13/05/2016)

Title: SBRI Challenge - Non Destructive Evaluation (NDE)
Description:
Develop an NDE technique with capacitive resitivity imaging (CRI) technology providing the capability to map variations of bulk low-frequency electrical properties within a structure and sensitive to any defects (e.g. cracks and fractures) or alterations (e.g. corrosion) affecting either electrical resistivity or dielectric properties of a material.
Develop the NDE technique in the following areas of military exploitation:
• In-situ evaluation of structural materials covered by sheathing, cladding, panelling, paint, tiles, flooring, insulating blankets, spray-on sealants or similar;
• Detection and monitoring of moisture and/or increased salinity in structural or building materials;
• Detection and monitoring of thermal anomalies in structural materials (without direct contact).
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59098-446144 submitted and held by Innovate UK for the Non-Destructive Evaluation programme. Key deliverables are:
1. Proof of concept that CRI technology is transferable from earth science and can deliver tangible benefits for military NDE; (20/11/2015)
2. A design concept for a highly portable and rapidly deployable CRI sensor array and instrumentation, suitable for in-situ military NDE; (07/12/2015)
3. A pioneering and systematic assessment (predictive simulation and experimental lab study using geophysical benchtop prototype instrumentation) of the CRI response to representative material flaws, reflecting those commonly encountered in military assets; (08/01/2016)
4. A detailed technical report including de-risking activities, rationale for design decisions, emerging characteristics of a likely commercial prototype, and details of route to market; (02/05/2016)

Title: SBRI Challenge - Non Destructive Elvaluation (NDE)
Description:
Develop an NDE device for helmets and rigid armour that will be able to detect damage using a remote handheld device to wirelessly inspect equipment in the field. The Acousto-Ultrasonics system shall provide a mechanism to compare received waveforms with a baseline (undamaged) signal, to provide experimental data that will be used in quantifying impact damage. The system shall be integratable to representative helmets and rigid body armours. Helmets will require 5 sensors per helmet, armour plates will require 4 sensors per plate. Faulty sensors shall be easily detectable and a suitable workaround shall be provided.
The work shall be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59640-446180 submitted and held by Innovate UK for the Non-Destructive Evaluation programme.

Title: SBRI Challenge - Non Destructive Evaluation (NDE)
Description:
Develop a technique to reduce inspection maintenance costs by deploying fully optimised guided wave inspections to quickly and accurately assess the condition of difficult to access fuel and hydraulic seals.
1) A reliable and repeatable operating procedure to assess seal integrity;
2) A method for accurately and quickly identifying mis-alignment and inadequate seal coupling;
3) An approach that minimises system disturbance and reduces prolonged inspection periods;
4) Increase availability of aircraft due to reduced, yet safe, maintenance programme.
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 61125-446206 submitted and held by Innovate UK for the Non-Destructive Evaluation programme. Key deliverables are:
1. Definition of pipeline geometries and seal types that represent a range of common aircraft fuel and hydraulic networks (19/11/2015)
2. Development of a functional three-dimensional Guided Wave Finite Element model (27/11/2015)
3. Development of a functional fuel and hydraulic seal model (22/01/2016)
4. Validation and testing complete with demonstration of a fully working prototype (26/02/2016)
5. Determination of a Guided Wave optimisation function (18/03/2016)
6. Demonstration of above and delivery of Phase 1 final report (22/04/2016)

Title: SBRI CHALLENGE - FUELS and LUBRICANTS
Description:
The work is to undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59574-444188 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Fuels and Lubricants programme.
Investigate the interactions of conventional and synthetic fuel composition on combustion vibration, acoustic signature and consequent hot-end stress/life.

The key deliverables of the project are as follows:

1.  Investigate the interactions of vibration, combustion instability,  and noise when burning fuels at a range of equivalence ratios on a small combustor and single can RR spey combustor.
2. Investigate the interaction of vibration, combustion instability, noise and emissions when burning alternative and baseline fuels at a range of equivalence ratios on a small gas turbine (APU) platform
3.Develop models quantifying the effect of alternative fuel composition on combustor vibration, noise and combustion instability.

Title: SBRI  Challenge - Fuels and Lubricants
Description:
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 61067-444228 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Fuels and Lubricants programme.
Develop a contact mode instrument to measure critical parameters of surface morphology which determine drag on military aircraft surfaces.
The key deliverables of the project are as follows:
1. Establish representative surfaces to be found on MOD aircraft and establish an experimental optical analysis rig.
2. Explore approaches and algorithms, down select candidates and develop to a stage where a prototype instrument can be specified.
3. Design, manufacture and validate a prototype on laboratory samples representative of military aircraft surfaces.
4. Validate laboratory results by testing on static aircraft.
5. Deliver a final Phase 1 report.

Title: SBRI Challenge - Fuels and Lubricants
Description:
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59597-444192 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Fuels and Lubricants programme.
Conduct a study and develop a model to enable evaluation of the effect of varying level and type of aromatics in conventional and synthetic fuel blends on system compatibility, fuel system life and soot/particulate production impact on hot-end life, signature and emissions.
The key deliverables of the project are as follows:
1. Investigate a selection of aromatic species and blends of blends for elastomer compatibility and particulate/smoke emissions from combustion devices.
2. Investigate blends for particulate/smoke emissions and heat signature from a range of combustion devices
3. Investigate correlations between elastomer swell, particulate emissions, smoke and aromatic species.
4. Develop a model to predict smoke, particulate emissions and seal swell.
5. Deliver Phase 1 Final Report and preliminary assessment model.

Title: SBRI Challenge - Fuels and Lubricants
Description:
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 60869-444211 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Fuels and Lubricants programme.
Demonstrate feasibility of a portable and efficient test system to support lubricant condition based maintenance. The project shall demonstrate the potential for a novel rugged hand-held external lubricant condition monitor.
The key deliverables of the project are as follows:
1. Experimental results demonstrating the degree of sensitivity to changes in lubricant viscosity analogous to initial degradation.
2. Experimental results demonstrating potential to operate sensor in wide environmental conditions without significant impact to performance.
3. Study to calculate operating performance of a hand-held field test unit. Including: battery life, weight, robustness, price differential versus laboratory unit.
4. Report on findings of the above points

Title: SBRI Challenge - Fuels and Lubricants
Description:
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 60979-444218 part 8 submitted to and held by Innovate UK for the Fuels and Lubricants programme.
To develop and demonstrate an advanced in-field analysis instrument for monitoring the condition of lubricating oil in MOD assets.
The key deliverables of the project are as follows:
1. A customised spectrometer which measures infrared absorption properties to determine contaminants and monitor chemical changes due to oxidation, combustion by-products or incorrect lubricant top-up.
2. Optimised sensors for integration within the sampling region and minimise sample volume requirement.
3. Software to compare and interpret the test values and issue guidance to end-users.
4. An appropriate housing to combine the spectrometer and sensors in an easy to use package and space models or similar produced.
5. Final Phase 1 report.

Title: GB-Bristol: SBRI Challenge - Non Destructive Evaluation
Description:
Develop a highly sensitive vapour detector based on an already existing technology, that can be used to assess the state of hydraulic seals and to detect fuel and hydraulic fluid leaks. The device will be able to detect trace levels of vapours (part per billion) and offer a more precise and accurate way of detecting fuel and hydraulic fluid leaks. It would also help to locate a damaged seal that is about to cause a leak. The device will provide instantaneous reading of the detected level of the targeted vapour and will be portable and easily deployable. It will operate on a 'switch on and detect' basis, with little to no maintenance and no consumables needed, therefore will be very easy to maintain in working condition. Because the sensor is based on laser technology, it shall be safe to the human eye.
 Identify the spectroscopic requirements of the analyser (e.g. review the fluids / fuel composition,Identify the target compounds,
 Perform spectroscopic absorption preliminary measurements, select the lasers,
 Assess the stability of vapours of fuel
 Modify a laboratory-based analyser and integrate the lasers,
 Complete a demonstration proof-of-concept of the prototype and
The work is to be undertaken in accordance with the SBRI application 59529-446169 submitted and held by Innovate UK for the Non-Destructive Evaluation programme. Key Deliverables are:
1. Intermediate Report: results and conclusions of Phase 1a (01/02/2016)
2. Develop and demonstrate a working prototype of the proposed system (02/05/2016)

Title: GB-Bristol: Land Vehicle Exercise (LVEX) SBRI Phase 2-Signature Reduction MOLLE
Description:
LVEx will contribute towards efforts to return to Contingent Operations by identification, prioritisation and evaluation of equipments and concepts designed to improve the Mounted Close Combat (MCC) capability.
This competition is divided into two separate strands. 
1.	COTS - Mature “Commercial off the Shelf” (COTS) equipment, which is ready to be tested in a military context will be considered. 

2.	SBRI - Novel concepts and applications, including COTS offerings currently applied in non-defence areas that require R&D to make them applicable to defence needs are sought in order to provide innovative solutions.

Ultimately this will help MoD to de-risk procurement, generate evidence of capability gaps and inform requirements for future Equipment Programmes.
LVEx 2013 focuses on four key themes. Industry is invited to submit COTS technologies with innovative applications, or concepts that could provide solutions to any or all of the themes:
•	Mobility - We are looking for innovative ways to enhance the mobility of our vehicles over difficult terrain. Platforms of interest are those of our vehicles weighing 40 tonnes and below. 
•	Signature Reduction - We are interested in solutions for reducing the visual, acoustic and electronic signatures of our vehicle fleet i.e. how easy it is for our vehicles to be seen, heard or sensed.
•	Weight saving - We are very interested to see solutions which demonstrate how technology could reduce the weight of our wheeled vehicles. Platform types of interest include all those vehicles weighing 20 tonnes and below e.g. Ridgeback, Jackal, Coyote, Husky, etc.
•	Stowage - We invite industry to demonstrate innovative solutions for optimising internal and external stowage across our entire vehicle fleet. Specific problems include: stowage of personal kit, stowage of individual weapons due to the lack of a universal weapon rack, external Stowage of fuel, Electronic Counter Measures and water (all of which will also require protection).

Technologies developed and equipment shall be evaluated and the performance and effectiveness demonstrated through the established MOD Level A-B-C trials process:
•	Level A – System Performance evaluation (paper assessment/system demonstration) 
•	Level B – Fight-ability (soldier field tests)/System performance capture 
•	Level C – User Performance & System Effectiveness (vignette trials) 

This MOD call for proposals will launch vis SBRI (The Technology Strategy Board) on Monday 16 September 2013 and will close on 23 October 2013 at 12:00 hrs. To register your interest in either of the two strands, go to www.innovateuk.org/competition-display-page/-/asset_publisher/RqEt2AKmEBhi/content/land-vehicle-exercise-lvex-2013

PHASE 2 ACTIVITY

 Phase 1 activity ISTEC developed the camouflage concept into a demonstrator suitable for fitment to a Protected Weapon Station. For Phase 2 it is expected that a prototype solution covering a complete platform will be supplied.

The whole platform solution will then be tested and demonstrated against current in-service camouflage to quantify the benefits of the system with respect to Visual, Near Infra-Red (Image intensifier) and Far Infra-Red (Thermal) signature. Radar signature is not to be considered.

Ease of application, replacement and maintenance shall also be considered with a focus on the simplicity of the aforementioned by non-technical users wherever possible. Due to the lack of environmental sealing, some consideration must be given to the effect of water saturation on the solutions weight, usability and fitting.

Whilst creating a whole platform solution it will be required to consider as a design exercise and feasibility study, the fitment of the solution to another/modified platform (TBD at kick-off), which is likely to be fitted with armour packs for theatre and/or may have a number of additional retrofitted equipment.
The contractor is expected to provide a prototype system.

Title: GB-swindon: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)
Description:
1.	The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department. 

2.	The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety.   As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3.

3.	The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered.

4.	It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system.  The new system should allow for a short, timed,  interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data).  In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area.  Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students). 

5.	The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality.

6.	The Authority envisages a need for a brief site survey to enable potential suppliers to inspect the facility and compile accurate measurements of the installation site. This is planned to take place on 15 Feb 16 13:30.

7.	The Authority has the desire for delivery and installation by the end of Mar 2016

Full details of the requirements for the Supply, Delivery and Installation of Safety Equipment for a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) will be included in the tender documents.

Please note it is MOD policy to make payment via Purchase to Payment (P2P).

Title: AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE EXTENT AND SCOPE OF THE PROBLEM ASSOCIATED WITH THE ACQUISITION MANAGEMENT OF SOFTWARE
Description:
DE&S are responsible for many systems that are software-dependent, i.e. without the software they cannot deliver their capability. Additionally, DE&S acquire and sustain many systems that have a software component. Some of the systems are software-intensive where software essentially influences the design, construction, deployment and evolution of the system as a whole. By this definition, any system is dependent on software.

It is estimated that over 80% of all new projects brought into core within MOD are heavily reliant on software to enable their overall functionality. The MOD through DE&S spends in excess of £1bn per annum on software systems that are critical to capability delivery. While there are some published studies, there are additionally many more anecdotal accounts of others, and the true extent, nature and cost of software issues is an unknown. The US DOD has undertaken some historical investigation into the costs associated with software within their acquisition process. To date the MOD has no quantitative information that describes the extent of the issue that software is causing across the MOD software engineering lifecycle. Therefore it is necessary that MOD undertakes a comprehensive assessment of software failures, liabilities and consequences including costs, in terms of resources to the MOD in order to invest in risk reduction measures.

Title: Technical Support and Development of the StanMIS Application
Description:
UK Defence Standardization (DStan) has developed a Through Life Standardization Management Toolset “StanMIS” to enable the implementation of processes described in JSP 920 “Standardization Management Policy”. 
StanMIS is a .NET web application incorporating tools to conduct and manage a number of Standardization Management (SM) processes to meet UK MOD capability, including: 
•	Standardization Management Plan (SMP) tool
•	Standards Requirement Verification (SRV) tool 
•	Interactive Defence Standard (Def Stan) drafting template
•	Standards portfolio management 
•	Decision Support Tool to enable intelligent standards selection
•	Ratification tool for the approval of NATO Standardization Agreements (STANAGs)
•	Watchlist tool for monitoring standards configuration data
•	Custom filtering and reporting tools
StanMIS is hosted on the MOD Intranet at http://mou.isg-r.r.mil.uk/StanMIS/ and there is a “cut-down” internet version which will be hosted as part of the DStan website at https://www.dstan.mod.uk/.
There is a requirement to further develop the toolset to meet new and changing requirements in SM and to refine existing processes. 
The management, searching and selection of historic (i.e. up-issued, withdrawn or superseded) needs to be incorporated for projects supporting legacy equipment and where project requirements cross multiple editions of the same standard. 
Additionally, a tool is required to enable UK Defence Standardization to better meet its legal deposit requirements and to support licencing agreements with third party suppliers of standards.
Further improvements to existing processes are listed below.
Scope of Work to be managed
The following additional features shall be added to the toolset:
•	A Defence Standards Portfolio Archive Management Tool.
•	A Legal Deposit Management Tool.
•	Improved Defence Standard drafting template and associated processes.
•	Through life assurance process for SMPs.
•	Improvements to report building and information sharing.
•	Improved management of Operational Datasets in SMPs.
•	Improvements to administration tools.

Title: Authoring, Cataloguing & Illustration Service for Maritime Technical Documentation
Description:
The requirement is to provide a continued, centralised, authoring, and cataloguing & illustration service for the control, creation, promulgation, amendment and or revision of the technical documentation that supports equipment and platforms of the Royal Navy and Royal Fleet Auxiliary.

The editorial service is to ensure all Maritime Technical Publications are produced in compliance with Defence Standard 02250 and CATSPEC 10 ensuring technical content is consistent with the information supplied.

Range: Illustrated Parts Catalogues (IPCs); Spare Gear Lists (SGLs) and Provisioning Schedules (PSs) in accordance with Def Stan 02250 Part 5 and CATSPEC 10.

Scale: The scope of this requirement covers a portfolio of: 7,500 IPCs; 16,800 SGLs and 7,500 PSs at a UK Security Classification of up to SECRET – UK Eyes Only.

The requirement consists of a core, regular service with a list of priced items to be called off by Authorised Users. These includes, but is not limited to:

CORE:
• Database Management Service: Produce and Maintain a Type B (Spare Gear List) database.
• Management of Illustrated Parts Catalogues held on the Line Item Database that is an MOD provided software tool.
• Handling and investigation of NonPatternised Demands on behalf of the Authority.
• Management of a PS library in electronic format that enables traceability, amendment and distribution.
• Maintain a unique reference number issuing service for all Type B SGLs issued by the authority under this contract.
• Provide an Investigation Report for each amendment to IPCs, PSs & new SGLs.
• Provision of, monthly, a Comma Separated Values (CSV) file extract from the Type B database to Surface Ships Master Record Data Centre (MRDC), this file is to contain the individual line item data for all upissued SGL’s within each calendar month of the contract.

NONCORE:
• Enact on behalf of Ships OC, the secure generation, maintenance, revision, amendment and publication of centralised cataloguing and illustration service for IPCS; PSs and SGLs that supports in service equipment and platforms of the Royal Navy and Royal Fleet Auxiliary in accordance with Defence Standard 02250 and Catspec 10.
• Promulgation of Equipment Introduction Packages in accordance with Catspec 10 as and when required/determined by the Authority.
• A Bulk Scanning service as and when determined by the Authority.
• Provide a Screening and Investigation service of all MoD Inventory based systems upon request.
• Enable Etask codification creation including obtaining the required mandatory information inclusive of monitoring the activity and highlighting any issues to the Authority.
• Any investigative work pertaining to the Core activities of the contract upon request.

Title: GB-swindon: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)
Description:
1.	The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department. 

2.	The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety.   As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3.

3.	The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered.

4.	It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system.  The new system should allow for a short, timed,  interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data).  In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area.  Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students). 

5.	The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality.

6.	The Authority envisages a need for a brief site survey to enable potential suppliers to inspect the facility and compile accurate measurements of the installation site. This is planned to take place on 15 Feb 16 13:30.

7.	The Authority has the desire for delivery and installation by the end of Mar 2016

Full details of the requirements for the Supply, Delivery and Installation of Safety Equipment for a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) will be included in the tender documents.

Please note it is MOD policy to make payment via Purchase to Payment (P2P).

Part 1 - System Safety in Action
Part 2 – System Safety Process Management
